findings.subject: toggle-group
findings.title: Angular single-select ToggleGroup throws on the server and aborts the change-detection pass
findings.description: HwToggleGroupComponent.ngAfterViewChecked runs on the server and calls core observeReadonlyChoice for every radio. That helper calls input.getRootNode(), which the @angular/platform-server DOM does not implement. Each server render of a single-select group reports 'TypeError: input.getRootNode is not a function'. HTML is still returned, but the pass is aborted: a sibling component placed after the group never ran ngAfterViewChecked (0 calls) and rendered 'after=0', against 1 call and 'after=1' in a control page using only a multiple-mode group. Reproduced with the published @hawiyah/angular@0.2.1, which is byte-identical to packages/angular/dist. Hydration in the browser afterwards showed no console errors.
findings.expected: No error during server rendering and no skipped lifecycle hooks; the new guide is a prerendered, hydrated Angular app. The React and Vue adapters attach the same guard only in effects/onMounted and server-render cleanly (<scratch>/audit/work/actions/out/ssr-react-vue.out).
findings.fix: Attach the read-only guards only in the browser (afterNextRender/afterEveryRender, as field-presence.ts already does, or an isPlatformBrowser check), and make observeReadonlyChoice tolerate a missing getRootNode by falling back to ownerDocument.

findings.subject: toggle-group
findings.title: Angular ToggleGroup loses its selection on native form reset while the model keeps the old value
findings.description: The Angular radios are checked through a property binding only and the component does not listen for the form reset event. After clicking a type=reset button, every single-select group in the form shows no checked radio, including read-only and untouched groups, and FormData no longer contains their values. The bound model still holds the previous value ('model=second'). Multiple-mode groups keep their changed values instead of returning to the initial ones. React, Vue and vanilla restore the defaults in the same test.
findings.expected: After a reset the visible selection, the submitted value and the component value agree. docs/nic-segmented.md:27-28 says Angular 'retains its existing value/CVA model'; React (packages/react/src/expanded-interactive.tsx:21 useFormReset) and Vue (packages/vue/src/expansion-interactive.ts:52) restore defaults.
findings.fix: Listen for the owning form's reset in the browser and either re-apply the current value to the radios or restore the initial value and emit valueChange/onChange, matching React and Vue; also reflect the checked attribute so defaultChecked is right.

findings.subject: link
findings.title: Angular hw-link hides its anchor: attributes are not forwarded and RouterLink causes a full page reload

findings.subject: toggle-group
findings.title: Angular control ids come from a module-level counter, so server output differs between renders
findings.description: HwValueControl assigns controlId from a module-level counter; ToggleGroup uses it for the radio name and the hint and error ids. Two server renders of the same template in one process produced name="hw-control-1" and then name="hw-control-2". Prerendered HTML therefore depends on render order, and the client restarts from 1. In the hydration test the ids were re-applied without console errors. Not verified: whether partially hydrated pages can end up with two radio groups sharing a name. React and Vue use useId and rendered identical output twice.
findings.expected: Deterministic ids per render, as in React (expanded-interactive.tsx:19 useId) and Vue (expansion-interactive.ts:41 useId).
findings.fix: Derive ids from an application-scoped source (for example an injected per-app id service or Angular's own id facilities) instead of a module variable.
findings.repro: node ng/ssr/ssr-actions.mjs: '[toggleSingle] pass 1 ... name="hw-control-1"' and '[toggleSingle] pass 2 ... name="hw-control-2"'. node ssr-react-vue.mjs: 'react: ... two renders identical: true' and 'vue: two renders identical: true'. node ng/hyd/check.cjs: 'hydrated components (ngh removed): true | console: none'. Paths under <scratch>/audit/work/actions/.
findings.verifierNote: Read packages/angular/src/forms.ts:6 ('let nextId = 0;'), :13 (comment 'Pass controlId for stable application-owned identifiers, especially with SSR.') and :17 ('@Input() controlId = `hw-control-${++nextId}`;'); interactions.ts:9 uses controlId for the radio name and hint/error ids. React uses useId (expanded-interactive.tsx:19), Vue useId (expansion-interactive.ts:41). The counter is module-level, so ids depend on how many controls the process has created; a prerender process that renders many routes will emit ids that differ from the client's fresh counter. findings.fix: Default defaultValue to [] when multiple, and decide in the contract whether a reset notifies listeners; apply the same in React and Vue.

findings.subject: number-field
findings.title: Angular NumberField silently changes the number being typed (-5 becomes 5, 1e2 becomes 2)
findings.description: hw-number-field binds the DOM value to the model with [value]="value ?? ''". While the user types, any intermediate text that is not yet a number (a leading '-', '1e') makes valueAsNumber NaN, the component emits null, and the binding then writes '' back into the input, erasing the draft. The next digit is entered into an empty field. With an existing value of 12, select-all and typing -5 commits 5; typing 1e2 into an empty field commits 2. The wrong value is emitted through valueChange and the form control with no error. Vanilla, React and Vue commit -5 and 100 for the same keystrokes. components.json marks number-field as verified for angular.
findings.expected: The typed value is preserved: -5 stays -5 and 1e2 becomes 100, as in vanilla, React (packages/react/src/expanded-controls.tsx:22) and Vue (packages/vue/src/controls.ts:203-207), and as EXPANSION.md:44-45 states: "NumberField delegates native input number semantics".
findings.fix: Do not write the model back into the input while it has focus and the draft is not a valid number: only assign input.value from writeValue or an external value change that differs numerically from input.valueAsNumber, and drop the [attr.value] binding.

findings.subject: text-field

findings.subject: field
findings.title: Error text is not a live region in any adapter, and Vue/Angular give no way to make it one
findings.description: All adapters render the error as plain text linked through aria-describedby with aria-invalid. That is announced when the field is focused, but not when the error appears after focus has left the field, which is exactly what the guide's Field example does (error shown on blur). React can pass a node with its own role because error is a ReactNode; Vue and Angular accept only a string, so the application cannot add role="alert" or aria-live to the message.
findings.expected: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA): an error message that appears without receiving focus is exposed through a role or property so assistive technology can announce it (techniques ARIA19/ARIA21), or the component offers a documented way to do so.
findings.fix: Offer an opt-in (e.g. errorRole / announce) or render the error container persistently with aria-live="polite"; accept rich error content in Vue (slot) and Angular (projection).
findings.repro: run-matrix.cjs, case tf-full in all four adapters: 'help <...hw-error> ... role=null' (collector also reads aria-live: null). Source lines above show no role or aria-live.
findings.verifierNote: Read packages/react/src/shared.tsx:34-35,68, packages/vue/src/shared.ts:5-6 and forms.ts:38, packages/angular/src/forms.ts:21-22,40; grep for aria-live/role="alert"/4.1.3 in docs/dga-*.md, docs/nic-*.md, docs/alignment.md, CONTRACT.md (no requirement found). Accurate statement: no adapter renders the built-in error with role="alert"/aria-live. React (error: ReactNode) and vanilla (author-written markup) can make it live; Vue (error: String prop) and Angular (error: string input) cannot make their built-in error element live, though both can point aria-describedby/describedBy at an application-owned live element. Whether inline errors must be live regions is a WCAG 4.1.3 judgement that depends on how errors are revealed (on blur vs on submit with focus management); the in-repo DGA/NIC references state no requirement. Not verifiable from in-repo references as a DGA failure; kept as a P2 parity/documentation gap rather than an established WCAG failure.

findings.subject: text-field
findings.title: Angular value controls take their default ids from module-level counters
findings.description: Every Angular value control (TextField, Textarea, Select, NumberField and the other HwValueControl subclasses) defaults controlId from a counter held in module scope; the built FESM has three such counters. In a prerender process the counter keeps growing across routes, while the browser starts at 1, so the ids in the prerendered HTML differ from the ids after hydration and differ between builds depending on route order. Because label for, input id and hint/error ids are all rebound from the same field, the associations stay consistent after hydration; the risk is non-deterministic output, an id change at hydration time, and anything outside the component that referenced the server id. The README tells applications to pass controlId when rendering on the server. I could not execute Angular SSR here (@angular/platform-server is not installed), so the hydration effect is reasoned from source, not observed. React and Vue use useId.
findings.expected: Deterministic ids on server and client without requiring an explicit controlId, as React (useId, packages/react/src/shared.tsx:57) and Vue (useId, packages/vue/src/shared.ts:15) provide.
findings.fix: Generate the default id with Angular's built-in id facility for the app (e.g. inject(_IdGenerator)-style per-application counter keyed by APP_ID) and pass controlId explicitly in every guide example.

evidence.quote: application-owned `controlId` when rendering on the server or depending on an ID.

findings.repro: Source reading plus grep of the built package: packages/angular/dist/fesm2022/*.mjs lines 24, 978, 1705: 'let nextId$3 = 0;', 'let nextId$2 = 0;', 'let nextId$1 = 0;'. Browser run (run-matrix.cjs angular) shows ids hw-control-1..N assigned in creation order.
findings.verifierNote: Read packages/angular/src/forms.ts:6,13,17 ("let nextId = 0;", "@Input() controlId = `hw-control-${++nextId}`;"), packages/angular/README.md:64, packages/react/src/shared.tsx:57,74 (useId), packages/vue/src/shared.ts:15 (useId); grep of packages/angular/dist/fesm2022/*.mjs. The built FESM has four module-level counters (lines 24, 978, 1705, 4804: nextId$3, nextId$2, nextId$1, nextId), not three; the one for value controls is forms.ts:6. Output ids depend on instantiation order within the process, so prerendered ids are non-deterministic across routes. Hydration mismatch not executed (SSR is out of scope here). P2.

findings.subject: date-picker
findings.title: Angular ids come from a module-level counter and change with every server render
findings.description: controlId, the dialog title id and the tooltip id are generated from module-scope counters. Two renders in the same Node process produce different ids (hw-control-1 then hw-control-3), and a client that starts at 1 will not match a server that has rendered other pages first. Angular hydration will rewrite the attributes rather than fail, but prerendered HTML is not reproducible and label/aria references change on hydration. React (useId) and Vue (useId) rendered byte-identical HTML twice.
findings.expected: Deterministic ids between server and client, as in React and Vue.
findings.repro: work/dates/ssr/ssr-probe.mjs picker: "ids render 1: hw-control-1 hw-control-1-formatted ..." / "ids render 2: hw-control-3 hw-control-3-formatted ..."; calendar: "hw-control-1-month hw-tooltip-1" then "hw-control-2-month hw-tooltip-2". work/dates/ssr/ssr-react-vue.mjs: "react: ... identical across renders: true", "vue: ... identical across renders: true".
findings.verifierNote: Read packages/angular/src/forms.ts:6, 13, 17 and overlays.ts:5, 10, 61, advanced-controls.ts:179 and 236. Did not run server rendering (out of scope). The counters exist (forms.ts:6 "let nextId = 0;", :17 "@Input() controlId = `hw-control-${++nextId}`;", overlays.ts:61 "@Input() id = `hw-tooltip-${++nextId}`;"), so default ids depend on how many controls the process has created. But the library documents a mitigation the finding omits: forms.ts:13 "/** Pass controlId for stable application-owned identifiers, especially with SSR. */". With controlId set, every DatePicker id (input, -formatted, -dialog, -dialog-title, inner -calendar) derives from it. What cannot be stabilised is the Umm al-Qura info tooltip id inside hw-calendar (advanced-controls.ts:179 "<hw-tooltip class=\"hw-calendar-info\" [text]=\"rangeDescription\">" passes no id), which always uses the module counter. Accurate statement: default ids are process-order dependent unless controlId is passed; the calendar tooltip id is nondeterministic regardless. The React/Vue comparison was not re-run.

findings.subject: tabs
findings.title: Angular hw-tabs starts DOM measurement during server rendering; the timer calls getBoundingClientRect, which domino lacks
findings.description: HwTabsComponent.ngAfterViewInit (runs on the server as well) calls observeTabOverflow without a platform check. With Angular platform-server DOM emulation, document.defaultView is a domino Window that exposes setTimeout but not requestAnimationFrame, so refresh() schedules measure() through view.setTimeout(measure, 0). measure() calls tab.getBoundingClientRect(), which domino elements do not implement, so a TypeError is thrown from a Node timer callback outside Angular's render call. Depending on zone/zoneless setup and whether the app is destroyed before the timer fires, this is either a logged error per prerendered page or an uncaught exception that terminates the prerender process. React and Vue only call observeTabOverflow from useEffect/onMounted, which do not run on the server.

findings.fix: Add description/defaultOpen to Angular (and a trigger association or documented pattern that sets aria-haspopup); make the Vue trigger slot expose attributes such as aria-haspopup to bind.

findings.subject: dialog
findings.title: Angular overlay ids come from a module-level counter, so server and client ids differ and change between prerendered routes
findings.description: hw-dialog (and hw-drawer through inheritance) default titleId and hw-tooltip default id are generated from a module-level `let nextId = 0` that is incremented at component construction. During prerendering the counter keeps counting across every rendered route in the same process, while the browser starts again at 1, so server HTML and hydrated DOM disagree on id/aria-labelledby/aria-describedby values until bindings are re-applied, and the output is not deterministic between builds that render routes in different orders. React and Vue use useId(). No browser globals or DOM measurement run at construction: dialog.showModal is guarded by isPlatformBrowser (overlays.ts:18,26) and tooltip/toast/nav-drawer DOM access happens only in event handlers.
findings.expected: Deterministic, request-independent ids (React useId at interactive.tsx:106, Vue useId at interactive.ts:82).
findings.fix: Use Angular's per-application id generation or derive ids from an injected per-render counter instead of a module global.
findings.repro: Source reading; no Angular server render was run here (delegated to the dedicated prerender task).

findings.subject: accordion
findings.title: hw-accordion throws during Angular server rendering and blanks everything rendered after it
findings.description: HwAccordionMotionDirective calls createAccordionMotion in ngAfterViewInit with no platform guard. On @angular/platform-server 22.2.3 the first line of the core helper throws 'TypeError: details.children is not iterable'. The error aborts the change-detection pass: only the first accordion item gets its text; every later item renders an empty summary and empty content, and a sibling <hw-table> declared after the accordion in the same template renders with an empty caption, no columns and no rows. renderApplication still resolves, so a prerender would silently ship the broken HTML. Tested with the published @hawiyah/angular@0.2.1 and @hawiyah/core@0.2.1 from npm (byte-identical to packages/*/dist). The other four Angular components of this family (hw-collapsible, hw-carousel, hw-table, hw-data-table) rendered on the server without error.
findings.expected: A prerendered Angular page must render every accordion item and following content on the server without errors; DOM-only enhancement should run in the browser only (afterNextRender / isPlatformBrowser). packages/angular/README.md:111 states the pattern for Dialog: 'A server render leaves the dialog closed; the browser opens it during view initialization.' React and Vue server-render the same accordion correctly (out/react-vue-ssr.log).
findings.fix: Create the motion controller only in the browser (afterNextRender, or inject PLATFORM_ID and skip on the server) and make createAccordionMotion tolerant of non-iterable children (Array.from). Add an Angular platform-server render test for every component.

evidence.quote: const summary = [...details.children].find(child => child.localName === 'summary') as HTMLElement | undefined;

findings.repro: cd <scratch>/audit/work/disclosure-data/ssr && node angular-ssr-page.mjs  (output saved in ../out/angular-ssr-page.log): "ErrorHandler received 1 error(s): [ 'details.children is not iterable' ]"; rendered HTML contains 'First title' true, 'Second title' false, 'Third title' false, 'row-value' (table row after the accordion) false. node angular-ssr.mjs (../out/angular-ssr.log) shows the stack: createAccordionMotion <- HwAccordionMotionDirective.setupMotion <- ngAfterViewInit.
findings.verifierNote: Read packages/angular/src/presentation.ts:46-79 and packages/core/src/accordion-motion.ts:13-16 (and compiled packages/core/dist/accordion-motion.js:5); grep for isPlatformBrowser/afterNextRender/PLATFORM_ID in packages/angular/src; read the server DOM used by @angular/platform-server 22.2.3 (third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs:3975-3980, 4865-4930, already installed under the auditor's work/disclosure-data/ssr/node_modules). Per task rules I did not run an Angular server render myself. Code confirms the hazard. HwAccordionMotionDirective has "ngAfterViewInit() { this.setupMotion(); }" (presentation.ts:60) and setupMotion calls createAccordionMotion(this.element, ...) with no platform guard; the only isPlatformBrowser guard in the Angular adapter is in overlays.ts:18. createAccordionMotion starts with "const summary = [...details.children].find(...)" (accordion-motion.ts:15; dist keeps the spread). In the platform-server DOM, Element.children returns a ChildrenCollection whose prototype defines only length, item, namedItem, namedItems and updateCache; the only Symbol.iterator in bundled-domino.mjs is on AttributesArray (line 4867). Spreading a non-iterable throws "TypeError: ... is not iterable", so every Angular server render of hw-accordion (or any details[hwAccordionOpen]) throws in a lifecycle hook. The cascade (later items and following components rendered empty) is the auditor's observation in work/disclosure-data/out/angular-ssr-page.log; I did not re-run it, but the throw itself follows directly from the code. The expectation (no DOM enhancement during server render) matches the adapter's own README pattern for Dialog (packages/angular/README.md:108-111).

findings.subject: accordion
findings.title: Angular exclusive group name comes from a module-level counter and differs between server renders
findings.description: The default groupName increments a module-scope counter. Two consecutive server renders of the same template in one process emit name="hw-accordion-1" and then name="hw-accordion-2"; a browser bootstrap starts again at 1. React (useId) and Vue (useId) emit the same name on every render.
findings.expected: Deterministic output across server and client. packages/react/README.md:38 'Stable associations use React useId, including during hydration'; Vue uses `hw-${useId()}` at packages/vue/src/display.ts:43.
findings.fix: Derive the name from a per-application id (inject(APP_ID) plus a per-injector counter service) or require an explicit groupName for server rendering.
findings.repro: work/disclosure-data/ssr/angular-ssr.mjs, output out/angular-ssr.log: '[accordion] pass 1 OK: ... name="hw-accordion-1"' then '[accordion] pass 2 OK: ... name="hw-accordion-2"'. out/react-vue-ssr.log prints deterministic=true for React and Vue.
findings.verifierNote: Read packages/angular/src/presentation.ts:44 and :87; compared packages/react/src/display.tsx:38 and packages/vue/src/display.ts:43. presentation.ts:44 "let nextAccordionId = 0;" and :87 "@Input() groupName = `hw-accordion-${++nextAccordionId}`;" - a module-scope counter incremented per component instance, so the value depends on how many accordions the process has created (a long-lived SSR process keeps counting; the browser starts from 1). React uses "const group = useId();" (display.tsx:38) and Vue "const group = `hw-${useId()}`;" (display.ts:43). Impact is limited: the name is only set by setupMotion and createAccordionMotion removes it again (accordion-motion.ts:37 "details.removeAttribute('name')"), and Angular hydration does not compare attributes, so P2 (nondeterministic server output) is right. findings.subject: accordion

findings.description: React reports per item (items[].onOpenChange(open)), Vue emits toggle(value, open) on the root, Angular emits toggled({id, open}), vanilla dispatches hw:change with {value, open}. findings.description: Every preview runtime is bundled at build time from local packages/*/dist through Vite aliases (React, Vue, Angular) or the pnpm workspace symlinks (vanilla runtime and all CSS). Nothing comes from the npm registry. At HEAD the local styles dist differs from the published @hawiyah/styles@0.2.1 tarball (verified against the registry integrity hash): extended.css adds "inline-size: fit-content" to .hw-button-group and nic-segmented.css adds an attached-vertical icon-button rule (commit 3ac5022, made after the 0.2.1 publication), and the generated preview-runtime.ts contains that unpublished rule. The downloaded project README nevertheless says the pinned 0.2.1 release "matches this guide". A reader can therefore see a rendering in the Playground that npm install of the downloaded project does not reproduce.
findings.fix: In the rebuild, resolve every preview import from the registry-pinned @hawiyah/* versions the guide itself depends on (one version source), and fail the guide build if the preview bundle is not built from those tarballs. State the exact version in the editor chrome.

findings.subject: #component/<id> > Playground tab (live editor)
findings.title: User code runs on the guide page's main thread: a long or infinite loop freezes the whole guide
findings.description: The preview is a srcdoc iframe with sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms" (opaque origin) but in the same renderer process and event loop as the guide. A 3-second busy loop in App.jsx froze the guide page for 3011 ms (longest requestAnimationFrame gap in the parent). An infinite loop would hang the tab with no way to edit the code. Auto preview is on by default and re-runs 650 ms after every keystroke, so a half-typed loop is executed while typing. There is no watchdog: the 4 s / 30 s "still starting" timers run on the same blocked thread.
findings.fix: Run previews out of process (a separate origin so Chromium site isolation applies, or a Worker for compilation plus a cross-origin preview host), add a loop guard/timeout, and make auto-run opt-in or debounce on idle rather than every 650 ms.
findings.repro: <scratch>/guide-audit/work/editor/behaviour.cjs (step A6) printed: "A6 3s busy loop in preview: longest parent rAF gap (ms): 3011 (>2500 means the guide page was frozen with it)" (log <scratch>/guide-audit/work/editor/beh.log).
findings.verifierNote: Read component-ide.ts:259 (sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms"), :326 (650 ms auto-run), :310 (ready timers). Playwright <scratch>/guide-audit/verify/editor/p1.cjs b (en, light, 1440, #component/button, React JavaScript); log <scratch>/guide-audit/verify/editor/b.log. CDP Target.getTargets and Page.getFrameTree to see whether the preview is an out-of-process frame. Printed: "B targets [\"page:http://127.0.0.1:4173/#compone\"]" (no separate iframe target) and "child frames in main-process frame tree: [ 'about:srcdoc' ]", so the sandboxed srcdoc preview shares the guide renderer. A 4 s busy loop typed into App.jsx (auto-run fired it) gave "parent rAF gaps ... {\"max\":4010,\"over1s\":1}" and a parent page.evaluate round-trip of 3418 ms while the loop ran; the guide recovered afterwards ("Preview ready | preview: after 4s loop"). The freeze is real in this Playwright Chromium 153 build; whether desktop Chrome isolates sandboxed srcdoc frames in a separate process was not checked. Severity lowered to P2: it needs user code with a long or unbounded loop and is a robustness/editor-design issue, not a WCAG, RTL, factual or primary-path failure; it is still a firm requirement for the rebuilt editor (auto-run of half-typed loops plus drafts lost on reload, editor-8, would lose work).

findings.subject: #component/<id> > Playground tab (live editor)
findings.title: The documented Run shortcut (Ctrl/⌘+Enter) also inserts a blank line into the code, and does nothing outside the IDE box
findings.description: CodeMirror's defaultKeymap binds Mod-Enter to insertBlankLine; the IDE adds its own keydown listener on the .hw-ide root that calls runPreview() without checking defaultPrevented. Pressing the shortcut in the editor therefore edits the file and then runs it: three presses turned 8 lines into 11 and pushed blank lines into the import block. The shortcut does nothing when focus is on the Framework/Language selects or Download (they sit outside .hw-ide) or inside the preview. It is only shown as plain text in the footer ("Ctrl / ⌘ + Enter to run" / "Ctrl / ⌘ + Enter للتشغيل"), with no aria-keyshortcuts on Run and no <kbd> markup (the CSS styles .hw-ide-footer kbd, but none is emitted). Same behaviour in Arabic and English, and at phone width (the listener is not layout-dependent).
findings.fix: Bind Run as a CodeMirror keymap entry with higher precedence (so it replaces insertBlankLine), register it on the whole editor region including the toolbar, expose it with aria-keyshortcuts and a visible <kbd> hint in the Run button tooltip/label.
findings.repro: <scratch>/guide-audit/work/editor/keyboard.cjs en|ar printed "Ctrl+Enter in CM: docChanged true lenDelta 2 statusLog [edited, running, ready]", "Ctrl+Enter on framework select: statusLog []", "Ctrl+Enter inside preview: statusLog []"; <scratch>/guide-audit/work/editor/misc.cjs printed "Ctrl+Enter x3 inside editor: lines 8 -> 11".

findings.subject: #component/<id> > Playground tab (live editor)
findings.title: Status announcements are chatty while typing, and errors are announced without their text
findings.description: The footer status is role="status" aria-live="polite" and is rewritten on every edit cycle: "Changes waiting to run" -> "Running example…" -> "Preview ready" (Arabic: "تغييرات لم تُشغَّل بعد" -> "جارٍ تشغيل المثال…" -> "المعاينة جاهزة"), i.e. three announcements per pause in typing with auto preview on. An error only announces "Check the console error" / "راجع الخطأ في السجل"; the console itself is a <pre tabindex=0 aria-label> that is not a live region (axe: aria-label is not well supported on pre without a role). "Copy file" overwrites the run status with "File copied", which stays until the next run.
findings.fix: Announce only run results (ready / failed with the first error line), not the edited state; keep copy feedback separate (a transient toast or button label); give the log role="log" with a heading.
findings.repro: <scratch>/guide-audit/work/editor/keyboard.cjs (MutationObserver on .hw-ide-status) printed statusLog ["edited:Changes waiting to run","running:Running example…","ready:Preview ready"]; <scratch>/guide-audit/work/editor/drafts.cjs printed "B6 Copy file: status = File copied" and "3s later status still: File copied"; <scratch>/guide-audit/work/editor/a11y.cjs axe incomplete "aria-prohibited-attr ... pre".

findings.subject: #component/<id> > Playground tab (live editor)
findings.title: Drafts are lost on route change, language switch, reload and on the Preview tab's Reset; visiting Angular changes the language choice
findings.description: Edits are kept per framework:language while the user stays on one component route (verified: React JSX edit survived Vue, TSX and back; Angular draft survived a React Reset). They are discarded by: navigating to another component and back (framework returned to vanilla, edit gone), switching the guide language (editor unmounted, tab back to Preview), reloading (nothing in localStorage/sessionStorage), and pressing "Reset" on the Preview tab, which clears guideSession and resets the framework to vanilla. Selecting Angular forces Language=TypeScript and the forced value stays when switching back to React (JSX edit hidden behind TSX). The Auto preview checkbox returns to checked on every framework switch (the whole IDE, including the Preview width select, is re-created). Nothing warns before work is discarded.
findings.fix: Keep drafts per component+framework+language in storage with an explicit "Discard changes" action; remember the language per framework; never let an unrelated Reset clear editor work.

findings.title: Diagnostics differ by framework: React and Vue run production builds that hide warnings, Angular runs in development mode
findings.description: The React and Vue preview runtimes are built with process.env.NODE_ENV="production", so framework warnings are suppressed: in Vue an unknown component <Buton> renders nothing and the status says "Preview ready". findings.title: The vanilla project shows a full index.html, but its <html lang/dir>, <head> and <script> are ignored in the preview
findings.description: For JavaScript (vanilla) the editor opens a complete document. The preview inserts it through a <template>, so <html>/<head>/<body> are dropped, <meta>, <link>, <script>, <iframe> are removed, and the <title> ends up inside the preview body. Changing <html lang="en" dir="ltr"> to lang="ar" dir="rtl" left the preview document at "ltr/en". An inline <script> in index.html is removed silently; an inline onclick handler is blocked by CSP and reported as "An external preview resource was blocked: script-src-attr", which is not an external resource. findings.fix: Either run the document as written (a real page in the sandbox) or show only the editable fragment; make the preview honour the user's CSS import; word CSP messages accurately.

findings.subject: #component/<id> > Playground tab (live editor)
findings.title: Opening the Playground for plain JavaScript downloads the TypeScript compiler (about 1.4 MB gzip in total); each run re-serialises up to 4 MB into srcdoc
findings.description: compile() always imports project-compiler (TypeScript, 3.53 MB raw / 983 KB gzip) even for vanilla JavaScript; together with the project-editor chunk (1.64 MB / 419 KB gzip, which embeds the vanilla runtime, all CSS and brand assets as a string) the first Playground open costs about 1.4 MB gzip before any framework runtime. Vue adds index.browser (compiler-sfc, 790 KB / 240 KB) and its runtime (279 KB / 91 KB), React 365 KB / 111 KB, Angular 1.66 MB / 436 KB. Every Run writes the full runtime into srcdoc again: vanilla 0.93 MB, React 1.39 MB, Vue 1.22 MB, Angular 3.98 MB per run.
findings.fix: Skip the TypeScript compiler for plain JS, compile in a Worker, cache runtimes in the preview origin (load once, re-run only user modules), and consider esbuild-wasm/sucrase-class transpilers.

findings.title: Angular takes 2.4 to 3 seconds per run, roughly six times React or Vue (machine under load)
findings.description: Medians over 5 runs on the production build (static server on :5410), with load average 11 to 19 on 4 shared cores: open Playground (vanilla, cold) 928 ms; first switch to React 470 ms, Vue 643 ms, Angular 3076 ms; warm switches React 335 ms, Vue 329 ms, Angular 2358 ms; JS->TS switch 607 ms; re-run React 424 ms. A second method that waits for the rendered DOM gave the same picture (React 485/465, Vue 460/222, Angular 2662/2608 ms first/warm). Angular is JIT-compiled in the sandbox on every run (and needs 'unsafe-eval'). On the Vite dev server opening the Playground took 2325 ms (median).
findings.fix: Precompile the Angular example (AOT) for the default state and JIT only edited code, or keep one warm Angular platform in the preview origin.

findings.subject: #component/<id> > Playground tab (live editor)
findings.title: In Arabic the toolbar is mirrored but the code/preview panes, file tabs and CodeMirror search are not
findings.description: In Arabic the IDE root has dir="rtl" and the toolbar, preview bar and footer mirror, but .hw-ide-workspace is forced to direction:ltr, so the code pane stays on the left and the preview on the right, and the file tabs are LTR. Focus therefore runs Run (far left of the RTL toolbar) -> index.html tab (left) -> code -> Preview width (far right) -> preview. Code content is correctly LTR with lang="en" (keep), but the CodeMirror editor element gets lang="ar" while its content is lang="en", and the CodeMirror search panel is LTR with Arabic labels and 13 px checkboxes. The status line mixes "Ctrl / ⌘ + Enter للتشغيل" without isolation; it renders in the right order in Chromium but has no <kbd>/bdi.
findings.fix: Decide pane order explicitly for RTL (mirror the panes, keep code LTR), keep lang on the content only, and localise/mirror the search panel or replace it.

evidence.quote: /* Pane order stays familiar while each pane retains its own text direction. */

findings.subject: #component/<id> > Playground tab (live editor)
findings.title: The "same" example differs between JavaScript and the frameworks for 7 of the 10 components checked
findings.description: The JavaScript (vanilla) project takes its markup from the guide's Code tab, while React, Vue and Angular use separate recipes, so the four views of one component often show different examples: Button: "Send request"/"Save draft" vs one "Click me" button with a counter output; Text field: "Email address" vs "Example"; Tabs: 1 tab list with 3 tabs vs 6 compositions (47 tab buttons); Toggle group: one "View mode: List/Grid" group vs 6 groups; Data table: one 2-row table vs a sortable 3-row table plus an empty table; Date picker: an Umm al-Qura picker vs an "Appointment dates" form; Grid: three "First/Second/Third service" boxes vs three titled cards. Select and Dialog are identical across all four; Portal header matches except the label language (separate finding). Adapter-level DOM differences also show up: React adds a hidden disabled input to single-choice toggle groups, Angular renders no hidden inputs for multiple-choice groups, Angular adds a skip link to the portal header, and every Angular example opens with "Console (1)" because of the development-mode log line.
findings.fix: Define one example per component as data (content, states, interactions) and generate all four framework sources from it, including vanilla; test that the rendered accessibility trees match.

findings.subject: #component/<id> > Playground tab (live editor)
findings.title: Little room for code: fixed 360/280 px editor below 273 to 535 px of chrome, dead space beside tall previews and nested scrolling
findings.description: The code area is fixed at 360 px (≥851 px wide) or 280 px (≤850 px) whatever the viewport height. Above it sit the guide tabs, the framework subheader, the IDE toolbar and the file tabs: 273 px at 1440/1024/768, 426 px at 390 and 535 px at 320. At 1440×900, after scrolling the demo to the top, about 7 logical lines of the button example are visible and the status line is below the fold; at 390×844 three lines are visible. Below 851 px the preview drops under the code (354 px further down). When the preview is taller than the code (Tabs: 640 px stage) the editor column keeps its 360 px editor and leaves 283 px of empty dark panel. Preview height is clamped to 320–1000 px with the stage capped at 40rem/36rem, so long examples scroll inside the iframe inside a scrolling stage inside the page (Tabs at 390 px: iframe 1000 px for a 1578 px document, stage 576/1029). At 320 px the third file tab (main.js) is scrolled out of the tab strip. No horizontal page scroll at any width (verified 1440, 1024, 768, 390, 320 in both languages and modes). The "Preview width: Phone" option has no visible effect below about 400 px because the frame is already narrower than 22.5rem.
findings.fix: Size the editor to the viewport (for example min(70vh, content)), let the preview grow with its content without an inner scroll, collapse secondary chrome into one toolbar, and drop the width select on narrow screens.

findings.subject: #component/<id> > Playground tab (live editor)
findings.title: Playground preview direction is tied to the guide language; the Preview tab's LTR/RTL choice is not carried over
findings.description: The preview document takes dir from document.documentElement.dir (the guide language). findings.subject: /#component/<id> (54 of 83 pages)
findings.title: The Code tab and Copy button show a different example from the one rendered in Preview
findings.description: Preview renders sample(id, "reference") while the Code tab, the Copy button and the Playground seed render guide.usage. On 54 of 83 pages the visible text of the two overlaps by less than 60 % (word-set Jaccard); only 12 pages match. Button: Preview shows "Continue / Secondary / Disabled", Code shows "Send request / Save draft". Card: Preview "A place for your next idea", Code "Request summary". Grid: Preview "Content 1..3", Code "First service...". The reader cannot copy what they see, and a control change is applied to two different documents (the canvas and a template of guide.usage).
findings.fix: One source per example: the live example, its code and the editor seed must be the same component instance/markup (render the example from the code that is shown).
findings.repro: node <scratch>/guide-audit/work/component-pages/codevscanvas.cjs -> "pages 83 text+class match>=0.9: 12 text jaccard<0.6: 54"; data/pages.json button:en CODE "Send request Save draft" | CANVAS "Continue Secondary Disabled"
findings.verifierNote: Read apps/playground/src/guide.ts 222 (data-guide-usage="${e(guide.usage)}"), 225 (canvas: ${inlineExample(item[0], preview(item[0]))}), 228 (${code(guide.usage)}), 294 (editor seed from #guide-code-panel pre code), 317-332 (updateCode rebuilds markup from guide.usage and sets every [data-copy]); main.ts 159 (preview = id => sample(id, "reference")). Ran p1check.cjs f1 over all 83 /#component/<id> pages, en light 1440: word-set Jaccard of preview text vs Code-tab text, hw-class Jaccard, and Copy payload vs Code text. Printed f1 {"pages":83,"jLt06":57,"jGe09":14,"bothGe09":11,"copyNotEq":[],"noCopy":0}; button canvas "Continue Secondary Disabled" vs code "Send request Save draft"; card "A place for your next idea ..." vs "Request summary Review the information ..."; grid "Content 1 Content 2 Content 3" vs "First service Second service Third service". findings.subject: /#component/<id> (API & markup contract, at least 15 pages)
findings.title: API tables omit adapter-specific inputs, outputs and events, and in places describe only one framework
findings.description: Hand comparison of 29 components with the four adapters. Missing or one-framework-only items include: tooltip - Angular names the text input `text` (required) but the page documents only "content :: React string"; dialog - Angular describedBy, titleId and the (openChange), (cancelled), (returnValue) outputs, React footer, Vue trigger/footer slots are absent, and the table lists "open / onOpenChange :: React controlled props" only; alert - Angular has dismissible, closeLabel (default "Dismiss") and (dismissed), none documented; menu - Vue emits `select`, Angular has triggerLabel, (action), (openChange), the page lists only vanilla onSelect and React items/onAction; accordion - Vue `toggle` event, Angular groupName and (toggled) undocumented; date-picker - notes describe React only while Vue uses gregoryLabel/openLabel/unsupportedMessage/calendarSwitchable and Angular gregorianLabel/dialogTitle/direction; toast-region - React getDismissLabel vs Vue/Angular dismissLabel and the `label` prop undocumented; text-field - Angular size, visualVariant, placeholder, min/max/step, readOnly and (valueChange) undocumented; icon-button - Angular pressed and (activated) undocumented; combobox - Angular validationMessage vs React/Vue requiredMessage, Vue resultsMessage vs React getResultsMessage; pagination - previousLabel/nextLabel exist in all three adapters, undocumented; tabs - Angular direction undocumented; link - Angular current undocumented. Heuristic totals over all 83 pages: 190 React, 268 Vue and 333 Angular real prop/input/output names never appear on their page (upper bound). Documented but nonexistent: `.hw-search-dialog` (search-field). Every page has a table (1-10 rows); 43 pages have no framework-specific notes, only a generic sentence.
findings.fix: Generate the per-component Markdown reference from the adapters (React props, Vue props/emits/slots/expose, Angular inputs/outputs/content slots, vanilla options/methods/events) instead of hand-written tables; keep only prose that cannot be derived.

findings.subject: /#component/alert
findings.title: Alert page states the danger→role="alert" default as if universal; Angular always defaults to role="status"
findings.description: The page says "React defaults danger to alert and other tones to status". React and Vue do this; Angular hw-alert has `role = 'status'` regardless of tone and tone defaults to "info". An Angular reader following the page gets a polite announcement for an error alert. The difference is not mentioned (the page has only the generic framework sentence).
findings.fix: Document per-adapter defaults in the reference, and raise the Angular default as a package gap (shared with the component audit).

evidence.quote: ['role', 'status | alert | appropriate static role', 'Announcement urgency; React defaults danger to alert and other tones to status.']

findings.repro: node <scratch>/guide-audit/work/component-pages/side.cjs alert
findings.verifierNote: Read component-native-guides.ts 155, packages/react/src/display.tsx 73, packages/vue/src/display.ts 71, packages/angular/src/presentation.ts 34-41, packages/angular/README.md 84. Ran p1check.cjs f2 on /#component/alert (en light 1440): role row and every "Angular" mention. Role row renders "role | status | alert | appropriate static role | Announcement urgency; React defaults danger to alert and other tones to status." React (role ?? (tone === 'danger' ? 'alert' : 'status')) and Vue (role: props.tone === 'danger' ? 'alert' : 'status') default danger to alert; Angular has @Input() role ... = 'status' regardless of tone. Correction: the page does not state the default as universal; it names React only. findings.subject: /#component/toast-region, cookie-consent, app-shell, calendar, portal-header, menu, popover (+ catalogue cards)
findings.title: Guide CSS restyles package components inside previews, so several previews are not what the package renders
findings.description: Preview containers override component CSS: toast region and cookie consent are forced from fixed to static positioning, the portal header is made to wrap, the app shell gets a minimum height, the calendar is stretched, menu/popover panels get z-index, ready-example toast regions lose their max height, and the dark surface for light/outline-white buttons comes from guide CSS. A reader sees a fixed toast/cookie banner as an in-flow box and a wrapping header that the package does not produce on its own. The rebuild forbids this.
findings.fix: Render fixed/overlay components in an isolated frame (iframe or a sized container with the package's own containment variant) and move any needed variant (inline toast region, static cookie banner, wrapping header) into the packages as documented variants.
findings.repro: grep -n "\.hw-" apps/playground/src/{expansion,demo-previews,guide}.css
findings.verifierNote: Read expansion.css 79-98, demo-previews.css 31-32, guide.css 19; packages/styles/src/extended.css 166, 169, 217, 222, nic-notifications.css 2-26, layout.css 62. Ran p1check.cjs f4 (en light 1440): computed style of each preview element, then deleted the guide rule from the CSSOM and recomputed; f4b.cjs read data-position/variant/inline style. Printed: toast-region before {position:static, overflow-x:clip} after removing the guide rule {position:static, overflow-x:visible}; the preview and ready-example regions carry data-position="inline" data-variant="banner", and the package itself sets .hw-toast-region[data-position='inline'] { position: static; inline-size: 100%; max-block-size: none } (nic-notifications.css 21). cookie-consent: no data-variant, package .hw-cookie-consent is static unless data-variant='banner' (extended.css 222); before/after both static. portal-header: package already has flex-wrap: wrap (extended.css 217); before/after both wrap. app-shell: min-block-size 192px before and after (sample markup has inline style "min-block-size:12rem"). The dark surface for light/outline-white buttons comes from demo-previews.css 32 and guide.ts 328 (finding 8). Accurate statement: most of these overrides are redundant with documented package variants; the claim that readers see a fixed toast/cookie banner or a header the package would not wrap is refuted. findings.subject: overview
findings.title: The home page restyles package components and forces light mode on its live preview
findings.description: guide-home.css overrides package component metrics inside the home: .home-request .hw-input sets min-block-size 40px and font-size 14px, .home-request .hw-progress sets block-size 5px, .home-feature-demo .hw-tab sets font-size 12px, .home-install-tabs .hw-tab sets font-size 13-14px, and .home-actions .hw-button sets min-block-size 49px and font-size 15px. The hero "LIVE PREVIEW" stage pins data-hw-mode="light", so in dark mode it shows a light card that does not reflect the reader's mode. As a result, the components on the home page are not what a consumer of the packages would get.
findings.fix: Render home examples with the package components as shipped, in the reader's mode. If a size variant is needed, add it as a documented variant in @hawiyah/styles.
findings.repro: tr "}" "\n" < guide-home.css | grep ".hw-" listed 15 selectors that target package classes.
findings.verifierNote: Read guide-home.css (split on "}" there are exactly 15 rules with .hw- selectors: line 2 ".home-actions .hw-button{min-block-size:49px;padding-inline:22px;font-size:15px", line 3 ".home-request .hw-input{font-size:14px;min-block-size:40px", ".home-request .hw-progress{block-size:5px", ".home-feature-demo .hw-tab{font-size:12px", ".home-install-tabs .hw-tab{gap:8px;font-size:14px" and "{font-size:13px" in a media query) and guide-home.ts:38 (data-hw-mode="light" on [data-home-stage]). Ran <scratch>/guide-audit/verify/shell-home/verify-p1.mjs (output in out-p1.json) in en and ar, dark, desktop: computed styles of the home elements against bare package elements injected into the same <main>. Accurate except one detail: the .home-request .hw-input min-block-size:40px override is a no-op — the package input already computes min-height 40px. The other overrides are real: package input 16px vs home 14px; package button min-height 40px/16px vs home CTA 49px/15px; package progress 8px vs home 5px; home feature tab 12px and install tab 14px. In dark mode (html data-hw-mode="dark", body rgb(31,42,55)) the stage keeps data-hw-mode="light" and its card renders rgb(255,255,255), while a bare .hw-card on the same page renders rgb(31,42,55). Severity lowered to P2: these are cosmetic overrides of real package components and a fixed-mode preview; the components still work without the guide CSS, so this is an honest-render inconsistency, not behaviour that depends on guide-only code (P1 criterion) or a WCAG failure.

The vanilla snippet comments "Enhance only application-owned HTML with data-hw hooks." and then calls enhance(document).

findings.subject: global search
findings.title: The shortcut hint shows ⌘ on every platform, and Ctrl+K is ignored inside any input
findings.description: Both search triggers show "⌘ K" whatever the platform. The top-bar trigger declares aria-keyshortcuts="Control+k Meta+k", but the handler returns early when focus is in an input, textarea, select or combobox, so Ctrl+K does nothing from the component search field.
findings.fix: Show the platform-appropriate modifier and allow Ctrl/Cmd+K from text fields (it is not a text-editing shortcut).

findings.subject: shell + foundations
findings.title: Very small text in shell chrome
findings.description: Several shell labels are 9-10px: the sidebar version (10px), the ⌘ K kbd (10px), the category counts (10px), the attribution on phones (.625rem = 10px), the home pill and proof row on phones (10px), and the token names on swatches (9px). All measured pairs pass 4.5:1 in both modes (lowest 4.54), so this is legibility polish, not a WCAG failure.
findings.fix: Use a 12px minimum for chrome text in the rebuild.

findings.subject: /#docs/vanilla
findings.title: The JavaScript article assumes a bundler without saying so; the styles do not load from a plain <link>
findings.description: The JavaScript article is offered as the "HTML + JavaScript" path, but its only setup is `import '@hawiyah/styles/styles.css'` and `import { enhance } from '@hawiyah/vanilla'` in JavaScript. The built stylesheet starts with a bare-specifier `@import '@hawiyah/tokens/tokens.css'`, which a browser cannot resolve. When the article markup was loaded with a <link> to the built stylesheet and a module script, without a bundler, tokens.css returned 404, --hw-color-primary was empty, the button had a transparent background, the font was Times New Roman, and the module import failed. The article never says that a bundler (Vite, webpack, Angular CLI) or an import map is required.
findings.fix: State the bundler requirement, or give a no-build path (link tokens.css and styles.css separately, or ship a flattened CSS file and document an import map). If no no-build path is supported, that is a package gap to record.

evidence.quote: f === 'vanilla' ? 'HTML + JavaScript' : ... 'Keep semantic markup and enhance only interactive controls.'

findings.verifierNote: Read guide.ts:51 and :64; downloaded the published styles-0.2.1, tokens-0.2.1 and vanilla-0.2.1 tarballs to <scratch>/guide-audit/verify/docs-articles/npm; served <scratch>/guide-audit/verify/docs-articles/www/no-bundler.html (plain <link> to the published dist/styles.css plus a module script importing @hawiyah/vanilla) on 127.0.0.1:5640; ran <scratch>/guide-audit/verify/docs-articles/verify.cjs Confirmed facts: the published dist/styles.css line 1 is "@import '@hawiyah/tokens/tokens.css';". Without a bundler my page printed primary "", button background "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)", font "\"Times New Roman\"", "404 http://127.0.0.1:5640/npm/styles/package/dist/@hawiyah/tokens/tokens.css" and "Failed to resolve module specifier \"@hawiyah/vanilla\"". The vanilla article and the "HTML + JavaScript" card never mention a bundler or import map. Severity lowered to P2: this is an omission, not a wrong instruction. The sample imports CSS from JavaScript (import '@hawiyah/styles/styles.css'), which already implies a bundler and fails loudly rather than silently. The published @hawiyah/styles README (line 13) states the requirement: "The stylesheet imports `@hawiyah/tokens/tokens.css`; a bundler must resolve the bare package import. For direct browser use, bundle once or rewrite that import to your self-hosted token stylesheet." The guide should carry that sentence or link to it.

findings.subject: /#docs/react, /#docs/vue, /#docs/angular, /#docs/vanilla
findings.title: Framework articles have no install step, no peer requirements and start with a repository-only command
findings.description: None of the four framework articles contains an npm install command or the framework version the adapter needs. Their first code block is `pnpm build:packages` plus `pnpm --filter @hawiyah/example-<x> dev`, which only works inside a clone of the monorepo. The peer dependencies are react/react-dom ^19.0.0, vue ^3.5.0, and @angular/common, core and forms ^22.0.0 with rxjs ^7.8.0. The Angular article never names a supported Angular version. Vue gives "Vue 3.5+" only in the lead, and React mentions React 19 only in a bullet about refs. A reader on Angular 20 or React 18 is not warned. The install command appears only in a callout on Getting started.
findings.fix: Open each framework page with: install (npm install @hawiyah/styles @hawiyah/<adapter>), peer versions, where to import styles.css, fonts, lang/dir, then the first component. Move "run the repository example" to a contributor section.
findings.verifierNote: Read guide.ts:62, :71, :78 and :85 and the ar equivalents (guide-articles.ar.ts:13, 18, 22, 26); read the peerDependencies in packages/*/package.json with node; ran <scratch>/guide-audit/verify/docs-articles/verify.cjs on #docs/vanilla, react, vue and angular (en, light, 390px) In all four articles the first heading and first code block are repository-only: vanilla "Run the example" / "pnpm build:packages\npnpm dev"; react "pnpm --filter @hawiyah/example-react dev"; vue "...example-vue dev"; angular "...example-angular dev". None of the four contains npm install, pnpm add or yarn add (hasNpmInstall false). The version mentions found are "React 19" (in the refs bullet), "Vue 3.5+" (in the lead), and none in the Angular article, against the peer dependencies react/react-dom ^19.0.0, vue ^3.5.0, and @angular/common, core and forms ^22.0.0 with rxjs ^7.8.0. The only install command in the guide articles is in the Getting started callout (one occurrence each in guide.ts and guide-articles.ar.ts). Outside a monorepo clone, the first command on each page fails.

findings.title: Article furniture is guide-only CSS and JavaScript that re-implements components the packages ship
findings.description: Apart from .hw-table, every structural element of the articles is guide-only. .guide-table-wrap (guide.css) copies the shipped .hw-table-wrap (components.css:250-251). findings.subject: /#docs/calendars
findings.title: The Arabic calendars article turns a component guarantee into a developer instruction
findings.description: In English, the out-of-range rule describes what the component does: the date is preserved and an explicit message is shown. Core does this: isCalendarDateSupported("1924-07-31", "islamic-umalqura") is false, conversion throws "Hawiyah: date is outside the supported Saudi Umm al-Qura table.", and calendar-labels.ts supplies the "unsupported" message. findings.title: Unselected radios display a selected dot until a choice is made (package defect)
findings.description: In a radio group with no checked member every radio matches :indeterminate (HTML spec), and the package rule makes the checked mark visible for :indeterminate. All five rating radios therefore look selected on load, in light and dark mode; after selecting 3 only radio 3 shows the dot. The visual state contradicts the programmatic state (none checked). Found through the rating template; it affects every hw-radio group without a default value (the component page shows the same pattern).

findings.subject: feedback (and the shared widget on content, cookies, participation, about)
findings.title: Page feedback widget imitates the package Feedback component and loses its visible selected state
findings.description: Every template, and the whole of the feedback template, renders a guide composition (section.hw-template-feedback, two hw-button elements with aria-pressed, a hidden form) instead of the shipped Feedback component (hw-feedback, Angular hw-feedback). The package styles the chosen answer through `.hw-feedback [aria-pressed='true']`; the guide composition has no hw-feedback ancestor, so after choosing Yes the Yes and No buttons are computed identically in both modes: the choice is exposed to assistive technology (aria-pressed=true) but not shown visually. findings.fix: Render hw-feedback from @hawiyah/angular and project the optional reasons into it (it has <ng-content />). If the reasons follow-up is part of the DGA pattern, add it to the package Feedback component rather than composing it in the guide.

findings.description: input-temporal.ts projects a DatePicker selection into month/week/datetime-local values with guide code ("Guide-only projection"). docs/coverage.md calls these "Guide recipe ... not extra DatePicker selection modes". Readers see working month/week pickers that no package exports; under the rebuild rule this behaviour may not live in the guide. The month recipe also leaves the picker's "Hijri · Umm al-Qura" switch available while always submitting the Gregorian month of the chosen day.
findings.fix: Either add month/week modes to the packages (all adapters) or show native month/week inputs; drop the guide projection.

evidence.quote: /** Guide-only projection of an accepted Gregorian ISO day; no calendar conversion. */
recipes; typed Gregorian ISO dates remain supported. Month/week projection and

findings.repro: node <scratch>/guide-audit/work/labs-journeys/week-keyboard.cjs -> en: after ArrowDown "Wednesday, 4 November 2026" {"hidden":"2026-W45",...}; node <scratch>/guide-audit/work/labs-journeys/inputs.cjs inventory shows radio "Hijri · Umm al-Qura" inside the month picker
findings.verifierNote: Read apps/playground/src/input-temporal.ts:19-30 (`/** Guide-only projection of an accepted Gregorian ISO day; no calendar conversion. */`, `if (kind === 'month') return date.slice(0, 7);`, ISO-week computation), docs/coverage.md:84-86 ("Month/week projection and time composition are guide recipes, not extra DatePicker selection modes."). node <scratch>/guide-audit/verify/labs-journeys/inputs.cjs (en and ar, light, 1440px) -> out/inputs.json The month, week and datetime-local pickers are package DatePickers whose selected day is projected by guide code into month/week/datetime-local hidden values. Each of the four pickers, including the month and week ones, offers the "Gregorian" / "Hijri · Umm al-Qura" (ميلادي / هجري · أم القرى) switch, while the projection always uses the Gregorian ISO day (date.slice(0, 7)), so a Hijri-view selection yields a Gregorian month. This is guide-only JavaScript presenting month/week modes that no package exports, which the rebuild rule forbids. It is disclosed in coverage.md and the lab hint, so readers are not misled about the package API; severity stays P1 under the stated definition (guide-only JS imitating a component capability).

findings.subject: /#inputs
findings.title: Arabic-Indic digits are silently dropped or rejected, and the lab never mentions the core normalizeDigits helper
findings.description: Typing ٤٢ into the number field and ١٠٠٫٥ into "Amount in Saudi riyals" leaves value "" with validity.valid=true (input silently ignored). Typing ١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩٠ into the National ID field fails pattern [12][0-9]{9} with "Please match the requested format." The DatePicker text field rejects ٢٠٢٦-١١-٠٥ ("أدخل تاريخًا ميلاديًا متاحًا بصيغة YYYY-MM-DD."). @hawiyah/core exports normalizeDigits, used by package controls, but the lab neither uses nor documents it, although its explanatory text addresses Saudi input recipes. Same in en and ar.
findings.fix: Document per-type behaviour for Arabic-Indic input (type=number drops it in Chromium) and demonstrate inputmode="numeric" text plus normalizeDigits for IDs and amounts.

evidence.quote: <input class="hw-input" name="identity" inputmode="numeric" pattern="[12][0-9]{9}" maxlength="10" aria-describedby="id-help">

findings.repro: node <scratch>/guide-audit/work/labs-journeys/inputs.cjs -> number ٤٢: value="" valid=true badInput=false | amount ١٠٠٫٥: value="" valid=true badInput=false | date ٢٠٢٦-١١-٠٥: valid=false aria-invalid=true
findings.verifierNote: Read layout-studio.ts:176 (identity input `inputmode="numeric" pattern="[12][0-9]{9}"`), :178 (amount `type="number" min="0" step="0.01"`), packages/core/src/index.ts:3 (`export { normalizeDigits, clampRange, sortRows }`), docs/coverage.md:103, grep of normalizeDigits usage. node <scratch>/guide-audit/verify/labs-journeys/inputs.cjs (en and ar, light, 1440px) -> out/inputs.json Reproduced in en and ar: typing ٤٢ in the number field and ١٠٠٫٥ in "Amount in Saudi riyals" leaves value "" with valid=true badInput=false (input silently discarded by Chromium type=number); ١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩٠ in the National ID field -> patternMismatch, browser message "Please match the requested format." (ASCII 1234567890 is valid); the DatePicker text field rejects ٢٠٢٦-١١-٠٥ with aria-invalid=true and a localized message ("Enter an available Gregorian date in YYYY-MM-DD format." / "أدخل تاريخًا ميلاديًا متاحًا بصيغة YYYY-MM-DD."), so that case is explicit, not silent, and is package DatePicker behaviour rather than lab code. The lab text never mentions Arabic-Indic digits or normalizeDigits. Correction: no repository rule or WCAG criterion requires these lab fields to accept Arabic-Indic digits (docs/coverage.md:103 treats digit normalization as application text handling; packages normalize only in PinInput and sorting/search), so this is a documentation/recipe gap for Saudi inputs, not an RTL layout defect: P2. Whether DatePicker should accept Arabic-Indic digits is a package question to record separately.

findings.title: Looping loader GIFs on the brand pages play indefinitely with no pause control
findings.description: The Motion section shows two GIF specimens that loop forever (NETSCAPE loop count 0, 3.6 s per cycle). They are specimens, not an indicator of an operation in progress, so the 'essential' exception of WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide, Level A) does not apply. Users without the OS reduced-motion setting have no way to stop them. The reduced-motion <picture> fallback itself works (verified: with reducedMotion 'reduce' the currentSrc is hawiyah-wordmark.svg / hawiyah-wordmark-white.svg).

findings.subject: rule-violation
findings.title: Guide CSS restyles package components, so demos are not honest renders
findings.description: 87 live guide rules select package classes, and 47 of them change visual properties: 40 font-size, plus radius, background, border, shadow and filter. They resize buttons, inputs, tabs, badges, tables and cards inside the guide, so readers see components that differ from the published defaults.
findings.fix: The new guide must contain no selector that targets an hw- class. Where a different look is needed, add a documented variant to the package. Add a lint check to the guide build.
findings.verifierNote: Quotes exist (guide-home.css:3,28; guide.css:7). I measured in the running guide at 127.0.0.1:4173 with Playwright. Guide stylesheets (identified by data-vite-dev-id) hold 106 rules selecting a class defined in published styles 0.2.1, and 67 of them set typography or box properties (58 font-size). On 13 routes, 25 of those rules matched rendered elements, including component demos. A stepper in the #components preview computed 10px versus 14px for the same markup outside it. A button in .foundation-preview on #foundations computed 11px versus 16px. My counts differ from the audit's 87/47 (different live-rule definition), but the claim holds.

findings.subject: rule-violation
findings.title: Guide reimplements components that the packages already ship
findings.description: 252 live rules, plus the TypeScript behind them, imitate shipped components: tabs (preview/code/editor and editor file tabs), table of contents (hw-content-navigation), toggle group, search field, toast, stepper, stat, description list, timeline, alert, page header, breadcrumb, icon button, select, switch, collapsible, badge, card and service card, footer and the skip link.
findings.fix: Replace each with the named @hawiyah/angular component (see the REPORT.md table). If one cannot do the job, record the missing input as a package gap.
findings.verifierNote: All four quotes exist. In the running guide: #component/button renders a custom .guide-demo-tabs[role=tablist] with no .hw-tab-list. Every route renders the guide's own .skip-link and .toast, and none renders .hw-skip-link. #apply renders .app-stepper and no .hw-stepper. Published 0.2.1 ships hw-tabs, hw-toast-region, hw-stepper and the .hw-skip-link class (extended.css, portal.css). I did not reproduce the '252 live rules' count.

findings.title: Literal typography, radius and colour values instead of tokens
findings.description: The guide CSS contains about 476 literal font-size declarations, 106 literal border-radius values and 126 hex colours (all hex colours are in component-ide.css). Category (i) allows only token-based layout and sizing. .hw-type scales and radius tokens already exist.

findings.subject: motion
findings.title: Guide motion is hard-coded, and a global reduced-motion override hides package behaviour
findings.description: There are 21 guide transition and animation declarations with literal durations, and none uses --hw-duration-*. The guide-wide reduced-motion rule forces transition-duration to 0.01ms on every element. This is not the Platforms Code motion the owner requires, and it would hide any package component that lacks its own reset; the static scan of 0.2.1 found none. The two keyframe animations (search dialog entrance, IDE running indicator) are stopped by file-local rules, and the live check with reducedMotion reduce found no running animation on 12 routes.
findings.fix: The new guide declares no motion of its own beyond package components and token-based transitions. It adds no global override, so the package reduced-motion behaviour is tested as consumers get it.
findings.verifierNote: not reviewed
