findings.title: Dialog: Angular always renders an empty footer and a close button without data-size; React and Vue do not
findings.description: <repo>/packages/angular/src/overlays.ts:6 (<footer class="hw-dialog-footer"><ng-content select="[hwDialogFooter]" /></footer> unconditionally; close button <button class="hw-button" data-variant="ghost">). <repo>/packages/react/src/interactive.tsx:163, :165 and <repo>/packages/vue/src/interactive.ts:117, :119 render the footer only when one is passed and the close button through Button (data-size="md"). The footer class has padding and a top border (<repo>/packages/styles/src/components.css:211) and is hidden when empty only inside the date picker (<repo>/packages/styles/src/date-picker.css:35). Census: "footer.hw-dialog-footer: more in angular" in 6 components (<scratch>/spikes/editor-runtime/project/out/recipes-census.md). The dialogs were not opened in this run.
findings.fix: Render the footer only when content is projected; use the same button markup as the other adapters.

findings.subject: @hawiyah/react, @hawiyah/vue, @hawiyah/angular
findings.title: Portal header: wrapper element, brand element and actions container differ between the three adapters
findings.description: <repo>/packages/react/src/expanded-content.tsx:92-93 (<div class="hw-portal-header-main"> wrapper; brand through Link -> a.hw-link.hw-portal-brand); <repo>/packages/vue/src/patterns.ts:151-159 (a.hw-portal-brand with aria-label, no wrapper), :166-167 (actions container only when the slot is used); <repo>/packages/angular/src/content.ts:63 (a.hw-portal-brand), :84 (<div class="hw-portal-header-actions"> always). Census rows for portal-header, portal-layout, site-verification: <scratch>/spikes/editor-runtime/project/out/recipes-census.md.
findings.fix: Define one header structure in the contract and align the adapters.

findings.subject: @hawiyah/styles
findings.title: No published page-level base: the guide's preview frame supplies its own body font, size, line height and resets, which changes 160 of 331 previews against the published stylesheet alone
findings.description: <repo>/packages/styles/src/components.css:1-11 (font-family, font-size and line-height for a list of hw- classes only; "Hawiyah components are opt-in"); <repo>/packages/styles/src/reset.css:1-12 (optional reset, no font or line height). Today's preview document adds body{color;font-family:var(--hw-font-sans);font-size:16px;line-height:1.65}, *{box-sizing:border-box}, button,input,select,textarea{font:inherit}, img{max-inline-size:100%}, dialog{...} and .hw-app-shell{min-block-size:24rem}: <repo>/apps/playground/src/component-ide.ts:221. A downloaded project loads only the published stylesheet (<scratch>/spikes/editor-runtime/downloads/hawiyah-select-react-typescript/style.css). Measured with the frame rules on and off, same stylesheet and JavaScript: 171 of 331 screenshots identical, 126 differ in height, 34 in pixels; DOM identical in 331; 35 of 83 components unaffected (<scratch>/spikes/editor-runtime/project/out/chrome-experiment.md, crops <scratch>/spikes/editor-runtime/project/out/chrome-diff/).
findings.fix: Publish the intended document base as an opt-in entry (for example @hawiyah/styles/base.css: font family, line height, text and canvas colour) and use exactly that file in the preview frame, the downloads and the guide; remove every rule that targets an hw- class from the frame.

coverage.notes: Angular offers only a directive, HwButtonDirective on button[hwButton] and a[hwButton], with variant and size inputs; no Button component, no loading input, no type default. React and Vue render a <button> with type=button by default. Enter and Space activation, tab order, disabled blocking and the focus ring (2px black in light, white in dark) were verified with real key events in all four adapters. Sizes measured: comfortable 32/40/40, compact 24/32/40, mobile 32/40/44 for sm/md/lg. Only primary, secondary and ghost colours were measured, so a11y is partial. React, Vue and Angular default examples are pixel-identical in en and ar; the vanilla example is a different one. Server rendering is clean and deterministic in React, Vue and Angular. DGA: sizes and adaptations are documented in docs/nic-buttons.md and dga.css; a loading visual is not verifiable from in-repo references.

The accessible name comes from a required label rendered as aria-label on the native button in React, Vue and Angular; vanilla needs an authored aria-label. Loading and disabled block activation in every adapter, and a click on a loading Angular button did not reach a host (click) binding. Targets measured 40x40 (md), 32x32 (sm) and 24x24 (sm in compact density, exactly the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum). Default examples are pixel-identical in React, Vue and Angular; the vanilla example is different. axe-core reported no violations. DGA: docs/nic-icons.md documents source 40px, the circle shape and density adaptations; official icon artwork equivalence is not verifiable from in-repo references.

role=group plus aria-label in all four adapters. Attached corners are logical: with dir=rtl and lang=en the inline-start button has radii 0 4px 4px 0, and with dir=ltr and lang=ar it has 4px 0 0 4px, identical in all four adapters, with a 1px seam overlap. Every button stays a Tab stop with no toolbar role, as documented in docs/nic-segmented.md; a focused button gets z-index 1, including the Angular hw-icon-button host. The default example is the same in the four frameworks and pixel-identical in React, Vue and Angular. DGA: ButtonGroup is described as a Hawiyah composition, so comparison is not verifiable from in-repo references.

All adapters render a native anchor. Disabled links drop href and get role=link, aria-disabled and tabindex -1; they are skipped by Tab, and handlers are suppressed in React, Vue and Angular. The data-directional arrow mirrors from dir, not lang (matrix(-1,0,0,1,0,0) under lang=en dir=rtl, none under lang=ar dir=ltr). The external indicator stays physically upper-right in RTL, as documented in docs/nic-links.md. Focus ring is 2px with 2px offset, black in light and white in dark. Keyboard is partial: tab order and ring were verified with real keys, Enter activation and middle-click were not. DGA: state colours are documented substitutions in docs/nic-links.md; RTL treatment of the Link Square icon is not verifiable from in-repo references.

Semantics match EXPANSION.md in all four adapters: single selection is native radios in a fieldset with legend, multiple is aria-pressed buttons. Real-key results were identical in vanilla, React, Vue and Angular: arrows move and select, skip disabled options and wrap; under dir=rtl with lang=en ArrowLeft moves to the next option; read-only blocks arrows, Space and clicks while staying focusable; Space and Enter toggle multiple-mode buttons, each of which is a Tab stop. Vanilla destroy removes the generated hidden inputs and stops toggling. axe-core reported no violations at rest in light or dark. React and Vue server output is deterministic; Angular fails on the server (actions-1). DGA: docs/nic-segmented.md documents segmented geometry and the focused-equals-selected colour as source behaviour; outline is a Hawiyah extension.

React and Vue Field provide context (id, label id, description ids, invalid, required) to Hawiyah child controls; verified in browser that a nested TextField receives required, aria-describedby and aria-invalid. Angular hw-field is a plain wrapper with a required controlId and no wiring. Label/hint/error computed styles are identical in all four adapters (0 differences across en-ltr, ar-rtl, en-rtl, ar-ltr and dark). Element tags differ: hint/error are div (React), span (Vue, vanilla recipe), p (Angular). SSR: React/Vue use useId; Angular hw-field has no generated id. DGA: required marker and error typography follow docs/nic-select.md values (10px hint, 12px error) which I could confirm in the browser, but the NIC source CSS itself is not in the repo, so the source values are not verifiable from in-repo references.

17 input types rendered through TextField in React, Vue and Angular (text, email, password, tel, url, search, date, datetime-local, month, week, time, number, color, range, file, hidden, checkbox): all produce the native type with label association. Focus indicator (border #0c111b light / #fcfcfd dark plus 2px underline, outline in read-only and forced-colors), reduced motion (transition none) and contrast (border 4.78:1 light, 5.78:1 dark; error text 4.85:1 / 5.22:1; hint 7.36:1 / 13.21:1) verified by computed style. Control height 40px, sm 32px. CSS direction is resolved from [dir], independent of lang: en+rtl and ar+ltr behave correctly. Angular ControlValueAccessor verified with reactive forms and ngModel (writeValue, disable/enable, touched on blur, reset). Angular SSR was not executed.

Enter inserts a newline and the value/payload is 'a\nb' in all adapters. Vanilla, React and Vue render 96px (the documented source height); Angular renders 122px because of rows=4. Angular lacks minLength, autocomplete, inputmode, cols/wrap and any attribute passthrough. Accessible-name gap for an unlabelled Angular textarea is inferred from the shared label template (only hw-text-field was run in the browser).

Native keyboard verified with real keys in all four adapters: ArrowDown/ArrowUp change the value and skip the disabled option, Home/End, type-ahead; payloads identical ('a','c','','c','a'). Chevron position and end padding follow direction, not language (35px LTR, 36px RTL in en+rtl and ar+ltr alike). The guide's six select cases are the same scenario in every framework, but Vue and Angular use raw native select markup for the multiple/listbox cases and the Angular example has to pass placeholder="" to suppress the built-in Arabic prompt. Checklist rows 50-52 (Dropdown) are recorded as Partial in docs/dga-checklist-review.md, which matches what I saw; a read-only state does not exist for a native select.

Addon order, radii and the joined focus underline are correct and identical in LTR and RTL in all four adapters (prefix at x=20 LTR / x=301 RTL; start/end radii via logical properties). The group ::after underline spans the whole group on focus (100% 2px) and takes the danger colour with aria-invalid. Angular always renders both addon spans; the empty ones are hidden by .hw-input-addon:empty as documented, leaving a 1px wider input (336 vs 335) when no addon is projected. A TextField with its own label inside the group stretches the addon to label+input height in all adapters; the docs say to keep the label outside, so not reported. SSR not executed; Angular uses afterEveryRender for presence tracking, which does not run on the server.

Step/min/max/empty verified with real keys in all adapters: ArrowUp from empty gives min (1), ArrowDown at min and ArrowUp at max do not move, 25 with max=20 keeps the value and sets rangeOverflow and :user-invalid, 2.5 with step=1 sets stepMismatch, clearing gives '' (React, consumer-parsed), '' (Vue) and null (Angular). Decimals such as 1.05 and 2.50 type correctly everywhere. The Angular adapter corrupts drafts that pass through a non-numeric intermediate state (see P0). components.json lists number-field as verified for vue and angular. A DGA/NIC specification for a numeric input is not verifiable from in-repo references.

Click/Space toggle, indeterminate (DOM mixed state, cleared on click), read-only click/Space guarded and value submitted, disabled ignored, tab order and focus ring (2px, black light / white dark) verified in all four adapters (rerun/choices.v2.log). RTL: logical CSS except the symmetric halo `left: calc(50% - 20px)` (nic-choices.css:27), harmless. Forced colours restores native appearance; reduced motion removes halo transition (rerun/media.v2.log). DGA/NIC: 20px control, primary check, focus outline match docs/nic-choices.md; deviations: read-only light boundary and dark halo.

Native arrow keys move and wrap, skip disabled, read-only radio groups block click and arrow keys while staying focusable (all four adapters). Group semantics: fieldset/legend only built in by Angular. Most serious visual issue: unselected groups paint every dot (choices-1).

role=switch on native checkbox in all adapters; Space toggles, Enter does nothing (native; Enter is optional in APG switch). Read-only guarded. Thumb uses inset-inline-start so RTL places off at the right and on at the left (all.react.ar-rtl.dark.png), matching docs/mobile-switch.md RTL geometry. Mobile density 52x32 track / 28px thumb measured; 200ms timing; reduced motion 0s; forced colours native checkbox. Shared findings choices-2/3/4/14/19 apply to Angular/React/Vue switch too.

Arrow/Page/Home/End match native in all adapters; in dir=rtl ArrowRight decreases and a click near the physical left gives a high value; lang and dir independent (rerun/rangedir.v2.log for en+rtl and ar+ltr). Read-only blocks keys and pointer in React/Vue/Angular. DGA: no slider entry in the in-repo DGA/NIC references - not verifiable from in-repo references. Guide example recipe identical; rendered differences come from choices-6.

clampRange enforcement verified in all four (lower End stops at upper, upper Home stops at lower, pointer at the far end clamps to [8,8]); read-only and disabled ranges blocked; each handle has its own label and the fieldset carries legend, hint, error and aria-invalid. RTL keys reverse natively with direction, independent of lang. clampRange throws RangeError for min>max during render in every adapter (consistent, documented message). DGA: not verifiable from in-repo references.

Native radio keyboard (arrows move and wrap, Space selects, no Home/End as for native radios), cumulative fill, read-only and disabled guarded, max clamps 0->1 and 25->20 in all adapters (out/p-rating.json). RTL: first star rightmost in dir=rtl and ArrowRight decreases; lang independent (rerun/ratingdir.v2.log). Stars 30px, 36x40 targets, 3px focus ring on label; reduced motion and forced colours handled. Form value: checked integer under name; once chosen it cannot be cleared (native radios, same in all adapters). Vue/Angular inputs lack hw-radio class and Vue uses data-selected vs React data-state; CSS relies on :has so no visual effect.

All four adapters drive the shared core transitionCombobox: ArrowDown/Up/Home/End skip the disabled option and wrap, Enter commits, Escape closes without clearing typed text, Tab closes without committing, outside pointer closes, aria-activedescendant/aria-expanded/aria-selected correct, hidden input submits the value, required custom validity works; identical in en/ltr/light and ar/rtl/dark. normalizeSearch folds alef/tatweel (ابها -> أبها). DGA: docs/dga-checklist-review.md rows 50-52 mark Dropdown Input "Partial" (expanded list visuals not compared) — no over-claim found; expanded-list visuals not verifiable from in-repo references. Alt+ArrowDown and IME composition not exercised.

Searchable checkbox list works in all adapters: filtering keeps hidden selections, Space toggles, repeated form values submit (hidden inputs in frameworks, native checkboxes in vanilla), required custom validity on the search input. Example content is the same in all frameworks but the shared example CSS strips the border in React/Vue. No in-repo DGA/NIC reference for a multi-select: not verifiable from in-repo references. Target size of 20px checkboxes inside full-width labels not judged a failure.

Enter/comma commit, empty Backspace removes last, empty Enter submits the form, remove buttons are named per tag (24x24 or 24x32 px) and return focus to the draft input in all adapters. Angular differs by an extra Add button (component, not example). DGA tags row 106-108 concerns status/classification tags (chip), not the editor: not verifiable from in-repo references.

One native input with inputmode=numeric, autocomplete=one-time-code, pattern and maxlength in all adapters; typed Arabic-Indic and Persian digits normalise to ASCII; CSS forces direction ltr. Required marker missing in Angular (cross-cutting finding). No DGA reference for OTP fields: not verifiable from in-repo references.

Toggle keeps the input node and value, keeps focus on the button, works with click/Space/Enter, is 40x36 px at the logical end in LTR and RTL (also lang=en dir=rtl and lang=ar dir=ltr in vanilla), icon contrast 10.18:1 light / 13.21:1 dark, ButtonText in forced colours. docs/nic-inputs.md maps the 16px padding; docs/password-field.md states no DGA node comparison for the eye icon.

Suggestions: combobox role, ArrowDown/Up wrap, Enter chooses active suggestion without submitting, Escape closes the list (a second Escape is the native type=search clear), clear button 40x36 at the logical end, returns focus, emits empty value; identical in all adapters and both directions. Clear icon contrast 3.08:1 light (alpha red per docs/nic-search.md) and 5.22:1 dark, reduced motion sets 0s transition. Default examples have the same six fields in every framework; preview heights differ (945/995/995/1011px) and were not attributed.

Same 11 cases rendered in all four adapters through the guide editor and driven with real key events (scripts cal-structure.cjs, cal-keyboard.cjs, cal-arrows.cjs in the scratch dir). Verified clean in all four: arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown and Shift+PageUp/PageDown; ArrowLeft/Right invert from computed direction and are independent of locale (lang=en dir=rtl and lang=ar dir=ltr both correct); arrow masks mirror by closest [dir], not by lang; weekStartsOn=6 reorders headers and Home/End; Umm al-Qura grid stops at 2077-11-16 with no throw and no arithmetic fallback (numeric Hijri fields come from the pinned table, Intl only supplies names); Latin digits in both locales (documented decision in docs/date-picker-ui.md); single tab stop in the grid; 48x44 day targets; 3px focus outline at 18.1:1 light and 14.5:1 dark; selected day 4.75:1. React and Vue server-render deterministically (ssr/ssr-react-vue.mjs). Angular hw-calendar server-renders without error but with process-counter ids. The pre-captured evidence directory had no entry for this id, so I captured it with the shared harness into work/dates/evidence/calendar. The React, Vue and Angular default examples are the same; the vanilla one is different. DGA visual comparison is not verifiable from in-repo references.

Same 7 cases in all four adapters (dp-structure.cjs, dp-behaviour.cjs, dp-focus.cjs, dp-forms.cjs, dp-visual.cjs, dp-misc.cjs). Verified consistent in all four: focus shows the ISO draft and blur shows the localized display; malformed drafts stay visible, set aria-invalid and custom validity, keep the previous canonical value in the hidden input and block native submit; valid out-of-range dates are emitted and submitted as ISO but invalid (as documented in docs/date-input.md); ArrowDown and Alt+ArrowDown open the dialog; Escape closes and returns focus to the input or trigger that opened it; Escape on the Hijri info tooltip dismisses only the tooltip; switching Gregorian/Hijri with the radio arrow keys keeps the dialog open and the ISO value; disabled and read-only block opening; label/for, hint and formatted-output associations resolve; trigger 40x36, close 54x44. Angular reactive forms (FormControl) work: required, calendarDate, reset, disable. The P0 is the Angular server render. Evidence captured by me into work/dates/evidence/date-picker (no pre-captured entry existed).

Default guide example is structurally the same in all four frameworks (div.hw-field.hw-upload, same label/hint, same FileUploadList composition); pixel differences 0.5-0.8% (noise). Verified in all four (default-test.cjs upload en): picker selection, FormData, native accept is only a chooser hint (c.txt is accepted, as documented), Space on the focused input opens the native chooser, removal buttons are named "Remove file <name>" with a 28x28 pointer target (20px glyph + ::after), keyboard Enter on a selected-file removal button updates FileList/FormData and returns focus to the input. Vanilla FileUpload is static markup (no controller). RTL: all CSS for .hw-upload and the list is logical; the native chooser button sits at inline-start in RTL. Native "Choose Files/No file chosen" text follows the browser UI language, not lang (native limitation, not a Hawiyah defect). Input focus uses the shared DGA underline treatment (dga.css:137-140) common to all text inputs, audited with the field family. DGA: docs/file-upload-states.md maps the uploaded row to decoded Mobile Components geometry (328x36, 4px radius, #F3F4F6/#D2D6DB) and tokens match (tokens.css:57,118,122); the official artwork/dropzone equivalence is an open item there and is not verifiable from in-repo references; the NIC snapshot has no file-upload selectors.

Exercised in all four frameworks with the default example (default-test.cjs file-dropzone en), custom sources src/{react.tsx,vue.vue,angular.ts,vanilla.html} (custom-test.cjs) and src/*2.* (extra-test.cjs, axe-core 4.14). Clean in all four: Space opens the native chooser; disabled input and ancestor disabled fieldset block drops in React/Vue/Angular with dragover/drop default prevented and files unchanged; the first-legend exception is honoured in all four; uppercase extensions (UP.PNG) accepted; native reset clears the input everywhere. RTL: extended.css:83-90 uses logical properties only; vanilla message language follows lang independently of dir (verified lang=en dir=rtl and lang=ar dir=ltr); React/Vue/Angular never derive anything from lang or dir. Reduced motion: transition removed at extended.css:292. Selection is not upload transport in any adapter (no network code). The evidence screenshots include a code-editor overlay artefact at the top-left; clean captures are in <scratch>/audit/work/files/shots.

Re-verified in all four adapters x {en/ltr, ar/rtl, en/rtl, ar/ltr} light plus en/ltr and ar/rtl dark with identical data (tabs-test2.cjs): automatic activation, manual activation (arrows move focus only, Enter selects), disabled-tab skipping, wrap-around, Home/End, vertical orientation (Left/Right ignored, Up/Down move), RTL arrow reversal driven by dir not lang, responsive overflow at a 320px container (7 of 8 tabs moved into the More disclosure), Enter/Tab/Escape/selection focus return, roving tabindex after a hidden selection (Shift+Tab reaches the visible tab), focus ring 2px black (light) / white (dark), 44px tab height. Results were identical across the four adapters except for the overflow default label. NIC mapping (docs/nic-tabs.md) values are implemented in nic-tabs.css; DGA visual fidelity itself is not verifiable from in-repo references beyond those NIC values. Angular-only extra input direction; vanilla additionally honours a disabled root/fieldset.

Re-verified with identical data in all adapters (nav-test.cjs, 16 light combinations + 4 dark): page window "< 1 … 9 10* 11 … 20 >", gap disclosure open/Tab/Escape/selection with focus on the new current page, controlled value echoed to the app, 1000-page jump input (min/max per gap, 9999 rejected with aria-invalid, 42 accepted), chevrons mirror with dir independent of lang, target sizes 40x40 / 30x30 / 40x30 (>=24px). Core getPaginationItems checked with edge values (pag-values.mjs): bounded output of 7 entries at siblingCount=1 even for MAX_SAFE_INTEGER pages, non-finite input normalised to 1, siblingCount clamped 0..5. SSR: Angular ngAfterViewInit uses only ownerDocument listeners, an optional MutationObserver and :scope/:disabled selectors which domino supports; no ids or timers.

No vanilla controller (static markup per packages/vanilla/PORTAL.md:24). Verified rendered DOM in all adapters: disabled items are span[role=link][aria-disabled=true] without href; separators are empty CSS chevrons rotated by --_hw-inline-sign (rotation flips with dir, not lang). Pure templates, no SSR hazards. Visual parity of my identical-data rendering is equal across adapters (shots/nav-*-*.png).

Non-interactive progress list in every adapter (no tab stops, so keyboard is N/A). Verified with identical data (activeIndex=1): complete/current(aria-current=step)/upcoming states identical across adapters; complete marker is a CSS mask check, others show CSS counters. Pure templates/controllers without timers or ids, so no SSR hazards. The DGA radial mobile stepper (docs/dga-reference.md:77) is CSS-only (.hw-stepper-ring in dga.css) and application-owned; not exercised here.

Browser-tested in all four adapters, en/LTR and ar/RTL (t-menu.cjs, out-menu.txt): ArrowDown/ArrowUp on trigger open to first/last item, Down/Up wrap, Home/End, disabled item skipped, Escape closes and returns focus to trigger, Enter/Space on trigger open and focus first item, Enter on item emits value and returns focus, Tab closes without focus return, outside press closes: identical in all four. Gaps: type-ahead only in vanilla; API shape differs strongly; Vue trigger hard-coded secondary; React/Vue items do not get the package focus outline. Items 182x37px (>=24px). Vertical-only arrows, so direction has no effect (correct). Default examples have identical content in all four frameworks; the visible trigger difference comes from the Vue component. DGA: docs/dga-checklist-review.md rows 61-64 mark Menu 'Partial' with exact visual states open; visual comparison with the DGA Menu reference is not verifiable from in-repo references. SSR: Angular ids come from a module counter (see popover finding). Pre-captured evidence PNGs show the guide editor, not the preview, so all screenshots were retaken under work/nav-b/shots.

Browser-tested in four adapters (t-popover.cjs/out-popover.txt default example en+ar; t-popover2.cjs/out-popover2.txt custom example with a following button). All four: region role with accessible name, aria-expanded/aria-controls synced, focus stays on trigger on open (disclosure), Tab enters panel content, Escape inside returns focus to trigger, outside pointer press closes without moving focus. Divergences: focus leaving closes only in vanilla; React closes on Escape pressed anywhere in the document and pulls focus back; React/vanilla render a visible heading, Vue/Angular cannot. Default examples: React and vanilla show a title heading, Vue and Angular pass only label (because those adapters have no title) - 'partly'. Placement uses logical inset-inline-start (extended.css:148), so RTL is correct. components.json lists Popover verified only for vanilla/react/vue (Angular built but not verified). DGA: no Popover entry in docs/dga-checklist-review.md or the NIC mappings; alignment not verifiable from in-repo references.

Browser-tested in four adapters with a 3-level custom tree including a disabled node, for lang/dir combinations en/ltr, en/rtl, ar/ltr, ar/rtl (t-tree.cjs, out-tree.txt). In every adapter and combination: forward arrow (Right in LTR, Left in RTL, based on dir, not lang) expands then moves to first child, backward arrow moves to parent then collapses, disabled child skipped, Enter/Space select, roving tabindex, 3px focus outline. Direction is derived from computed direction (core getDirection, packages/core/src/index.ts:178), never from locale. Divergences: Vue has no indentation; React/Vue toggles render as unstyled UA buttons while Angular uses span.hw-tree-toggle; React toggle names hard-coded English; type-ahead only in vanilla; React does not wrap at ends while the others do; API naming and form participation differ. Default example content is the same in all frameworks (vanilla uses its own toggle icon markup). Selected node light 4.54:1, dark 5.84:1 (alpha-composited) text contrast. Suitability: TreeView is a selection widget (treeitems are not links, no href), so it is not a drop-in documentation sidebar; a sidebar needs link items or plain nested nav lists. DGA: no TreeView entry in in-repo DGA/NIC references - not verifiable.

Browser-tested in four adapters (t-cnav.cjs/out-cnav.txt, t-cnav-flicker.cjs/out-cnav-flicker.txt), en and ar, reducedMotion reduce and no-preference: initial current = first section; scrolling the bounded root updates aria-current=location; scroll end activates last section; click scrolls only the local root (window scrollY stays 0, URL hash unchanged); reduce => instant (scrollTop at target immediately), no-preference => smooth; keyboard Enter focuses the section with temporary tabindex=-1 removed on blur; disabled destination inert in all four (vanilla authored <a aria-disabled tabindex=-1>, frameworks <span role=link aria-disabled>). Link 335x40px. Contrast: active marker 4.75:1 light / 6.43:1 dark against the nav background; focus outline 2px black/white. Observer cleanup verified by code: core destroy() removes scroll/resize/fonts listeners, disconnects Mutation/ResizeObserver, cancels pending frame and restores temporary tabindex (content-navigation.ts:148-159); React effect cleanup, Vue onBeforeUnmount, Angular ngOnDestroy, vanilla scope. Offset verified from code only (threshold offset+20, navigate subtracts offset). DGA/NIC: geometry and states match docs/nic-content-navigation.md (40px link height measured, 3px marker, 2px rail, focus outline kept as documented adaptation). Examples: same items and structure in four frameworks; vanilla scroll root adds border-radius and scroll-padding inline styles the frameworks lack ('partly'). Suitability: good for an on-page table of contents within one document (nested lists, aria-current, bounded or window scroll, sticky >=1200px); not a cross-page documentation sidebar (only section ids, click always intercepted, no href/route items, no URL fragment update).

Native showModal in all four adapters. Verified in every adapter (out/02-dialog*.log): initial focus on the close button, Tab/Shift+Tab stay inside, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger, backdrop click closes, drag inside->outside, drag outside->inside and right-click do not close (EXPANSION.md gesture rule), header close, method=dialog form and footer close all return focus and sync controlled state/events. In a top-level page Tab past the last control goes to browser UI then back into the dialog (native behaviour, not a trap). Reduced motion removes the entrance animation; focus ring 2px solid black/white; forced colours keep border. NIC notification-dialog geometry (docs/nic-notifications.md) was not re-measured.

guide:tests.summary:
REPORT.md was not written: the harness rejected the Write call for a report file ("Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files"), and I did not work around it. The full detail is in this result; the generated data files are in <scratch>/guide-audit/work/tests/ (reportPath points at the complete per-file table for tests/browser, which a script had already produced). Neither Playwright suite nor Vitest was run (shared machine, load average above 20); tests were listed with `playwright test --list` and `vitest list` and read. Nothing in the repository was modified.

A. Inventory and classes. tests/browser has 81 spec files and 531 tests (the directory has 83 entries: 81 specs, the manual script framework-calendars.mjs and support/). Per test: class 1 (package behaviour or styling through the guide) 435, class 2 (guide behaviour) 69, class 3 (templates and journeys) 21, class 4 (brand and assets) 6. Per file: 55 purely class 1, 11 class 2, 4 class 3, 1 class 4, 10 mixed. tests/frameworks has 18 files and 27 tests, each run in three projects (81 runs); all are class 1 and hosted in the example apps, not the guide. Unit level: 117 Vitest files (461 static entries, 75 of them parameterised; docs/validation.md records 637 cases) plus the token contrast node test.

B. Coupling. Host of the 435 class-1 tests: live editor iframe 317 (vanilla 67, React 98, Vue 98, Angular 54), guide component page 57, markup injected into a guide page 32, lab or catalogue page 22, neutral setContent page 7. So 428 lose their page when the guide is replaced and the other 7 lose a stylesheet import from a guide-generated module. Selectors involved: [data-guide-tab="playground"], [data-project-framework], [data-project-language], .hw-ide-status, .hw-ide-frame, .hw-ide-console, [data-ide-*], .component-preview, #component-examples, [data-guide-canvas], .guide-preview, [data-demo-result], hash routes #component/<id>. A neutral host needs: one fixture app per adapter on the published packages with only @hawiyah/styles/styles.css; one URL per component example with locale, direction, mode, theme and density as separate parameters; one shared example registry (today apps/playground/src/project-examples.ts); neutral data-testid hooks as in tests/frameworks; a blank page with the package stylesheet; a real module URL for @hawiyah/vanilla; no host CSS that touches components.

C. Adapter coverage. Render smoke exists for all 83 components in all four adapters (project-editor.spec.ts). Beyond that, components with neither a unit reference nor a dedicated browser assertion: vanilla 16, React 8, Vue 8, Angular 7; empty-state, description-list, stat and meter have none in any adapter. components.json: 182 evidence entries, all files exist; 252 of 254 cited titles match a real test, 2 do not; 53 tested component and adapter pairs are not marked verified; 40 evidence entries cite guide-hosted specs.

D. CI. pages.yml (push to main, manual) builds and deploys the guide; publish.yml (version tag, manual) builds, runs the clean-consumer tarball check and publishes. No workflow runs Vitest, the contrast test, either Playwright suite or the editor-project check, and none is triggered by pull requests. Deployment and publication are not gated on any test.

E. Accessibility, direction, motion. 41 axe call sites in 33 files, none with suppressed rules; three different rule sets (4 sites with WCAG 2.2 AA tags, 9 with wcag2a and wcag2aa only, 28 default). Whole-page scans cover 6 guide routes in English light and Arabic dark only. 51 files set or assert direction; locale and direction apart is asserted for packages, not for the guide. 45 files emulate reduced motion and 34 forced colours; a guide-only global reduced-motion rule masks four of the reduced-motion assertions (reproduced). Dark mode is reachable only through localStorage.

F. Migration. Keep the unit and parity tests, tests/frameworks, the Locator-scoped helper library and the 83 by 7 smoke enumeration, and re-point the 428 guide-hosted package tests at a four-adapter fixture host. Port the class-2 intents (shell, search, navigation, reflow, whole-page axe, content completeness, install commands, link containment, editor sandbox) to the Angular guide with new selectors. Retire tests of guide-only CSS and of the guide-only copy action. A matrix built from what exists: static checks; parameterised unit tests; 83 x 4 x 2 fixture smoke with axe (664 renders); fixture behaviour specs run as four Playwright projects; guide tests; templates; and the same fixture tiers against registry versions before release.

Data files in the scratch directory: table-browser.md (per-file table), browser-list.tsv, portals-list.tsv, vitest-list.json, class-counts.json, coupling.json, matrix.tsv, matrix-gaps.json, evidence-check.tsv, a11y.json, probe.out, probe-motion.out, and the scripts that produced them.

guide:editor.summary: The live editor works and is well isolated (opaque-origin sandbox and CSP blocked every probe; Tab leaves CodeMirror; code stays LTR in Arabic), but it is not an honest render of the published packages and it is heavy and fragile. Previews are bundled from local packages/*/dist, which already differ from @hawiyah/styles@0.2.1, while the download README says the 0.2.1 release "matches this guide" and docs/editor-projects.md still calls the packages unpublished. User code runs on the guide's main thread (a 3 s loop froze the page for 3011 ms), auto-run fires 650 ms after each keystroke, and the Ctrl/Cmd+Enter shortcut also inserts a blank line. English portal-header examples show Arabic labels in all three framework adapters. 7 of 10 components show a different example in JavaScript than in React/Vue/Angular, and recipe sources have lines of up to 5,887 characters. The code gets a fixed 360/280 px under 273-535 px of chrome; drafts vanish on route/language change, reload or the Preview tab's Reset. Opening the editor loads about 1.4 MB gzip (TypeScript compiler even for plain JS); Angular takes about 2.4-3 s per run versus 0.2-0.6 s for React/Vue (machine under load). Downloads pin 0.2.1 and framework versions that all exist in the registry (install not run). Redesign: A fixes chrome and space but not architecture; B suits component pages and phones; C suits only a dedicated full-width route. Recommended: B on component pages with one shared example per component, plus a separate full-width editor (A toolbar, C log, no file tree) running registry packages out of process.
keep: Unique-origin sandbox (no allow-same-origin) with the two-policy CSP: parent DOM, top navigation, storage, cookies, popups, eval and network were all blocked in the probe, and errors stayed in the editor log.
Code stays LTR with lang="en" inside Arabic chrome; the log uses unicode-bidi: plaintext so Arabic log lines keep their own direction.
Tab leaves CodeMirror (no keyboard trap); file tabs are a roving tablist with arrow/Home/End keys; visible focus outlines with at least 5:1 contrast; reduced-motion handling of the status animation.
Per framework:language drafts within a visit, Reset that only affects the current combination and can be undone with Ctrl+Z.
Real per-framework entry points (createRoot, createApp, bootstrapApplication) and downloadable projects whose manifests resolve from the registry.
Select and Dialog recipes, which are identical across all four frameworks: the model for every other component.
Localized CodeMirror phrases for Arabic and translated status/log messages.

Running user code in a same-process srcdoc iframe without a loop guard; auto-run every 650 ms.
The guide-only .hw-ide-* chrome and hard-coded hex palette (component-ide.css, 587 lines).
The second toolbar, the decorative "Component workspace" block, the guide-level Copy that copies vanilla markup, and the native Framework/Language selects labelled "JavaScript"/"JavaScript".
Ctrl/Cmd+Enter bound outside CodeMirror's keymap.
String-concatenated one-line example sources; separate vanilla vs framework examples.
Silent 40-line console truncation and bundle-relative error positions.
The full vanilla index.html whose <html>/<head>/<script> are ignored; stripping the user's @import while always injecting styles.
The "Real components. Real interaction." tagline and the stale docs/editor-projects.md history.

pros: Removes the two-toolbar stack (guide tabs + subheader + IDE toolbar = 273 px above code at desktop, 535 px at 320 px) and frees roughly 150-250 px for code
Segmented framework/language controls make the 4 frameworks and the Angular TypeScript-only rule visible at once (today a disabled native select)
Run with a shown shortcut fixes discoverability if the shortcut is bound in CodeMirror's keymap (today it inserts a blank line)
A thin status bar can carry version, state and error count in one line
cons: Icon-only actions need tooltips and accessible names in both languages; at 320 px four frameworks + two languages + actions still need two rows or an overflow menu
Keeps the code-first layout, so on phones the result remains far below the code
Does not by itself fix drafts, the main-thread sandbox or example quality
risks: Segmented control, toolbar and icon-button-with-tooltip must exist in @hawiyah/angular first (the rebuild forbids guide-only imitations)
Mis-sized toolbar wrapping in Arabic if labels are long; must test 320 px in both languages

pros: Matches what most readers want on a component page: the result first, code on demand
Phone layout becomes natural (result at the top, collapsible code below); removes nested result scrolling if the preview grows with content
Framework tabs over the code make the cross-framework comparison explicit and push the team toward one shared example
cons: Editing and watching the result at the same time is harder on desktop (scroll between them) unless the code panel is tall and sticky
Collapsed code hides the editor from keyboard users unless the disclosure is clearly labelled and remembered
risks: If the brief component page also has a static example, preview-first editor duplicates it (the owner's one-fact-one-place rule); the editor should replace, not repeat, the page example
Auto-run while typing would make the preview jump above the caret; needs explicit Run or run-on-idle

pros: Best for multi-file recipes (dialog 52-61 lines, date-picker 24-32 lines) and for the downloaded project mental model (file tree = ZIP contents)
Side-by-side editor/result with a log panel suits wide screens and a dedicated full-page route
cons: Heaviest UI: side panel + file tree + editor + result + log cannot fit inside a component page column (886 px wide at 1440) or a phone
Most examples are 3 files of which only one is interesting; a file tree adds navigation for little content
risks: Building a file tree, splitter and log as package components is a large new surface for the libraries
Same main-thread and payload problems unless the runtime architecture changes (TypeScript compiler 983 KB gzip, Angular 436 KB gzip, 4 MB srcdoc per Angular run)

redesign_directions.D_recommended: Split the job: on component pages use B (result first, read-only formatted source per framework from one shared example definition, copy and "Open in editor"), and keep a full-width editor route using A's single toolbar with C's log panel but without a file tree (file tabs suffice). Run user code in a separate-origin preview host (or a Worker for compilation) with a loop guard, load registry-pinned @hawiyah packages, persist drafts per component/framework/language, and give the editor its own locale and direction controls. This keeps the editor light on the 83 component pages (no 1.4 MB gzip compiler until the user asks to edit) and moves the heavy parts to one route.

guide:component-pages.summary: The catalogue and the 83 component pages render real @hawiyah/styles and @hawiyah/vanilla components, reflow at 390 and 320px (sampled 14 pages, en/ar), pass axe contrast in light and dark, keep visible focus, and contain no prohibited claims. The main problems: the Code tab, Copy button and editor seed show a different example from the Preview on 54 of 83 pages; guide CSS repositions or restyles several components inside previews (toast region, cookie consent, portal header, app shell, calendar, on-dark buttons); API tables omit or misattribute adapter-specific API on at least 15 of 29 hand-checked components (Angular tooltip text, dialog/alert/menu/accordion outputs, Angular alert role default); pages are long (median 454 words, 3691px) with about a third verbatim boilerplate on every page and 58 % of words repeated elsewhere; and on the catalogue, category chips and Reset drop focus to <body>, and the page scrolls horizontally at 320px because of the upload preview. Headings are slogan-style in both languages and the Arabic headings are not translations of the English.
keep: Live, real package rendering of every component (vanilla + @hawiyah/styles) with no console errors on any of the 166 page loads; in the rebuild, the Angular component from npm.
The Direction control (RTL/LTR) that sets the preview direction independently of the page locale, with aria-pressed state (guide.ts:226, verified).
Accessible tab pattern for Preview/Code/Playground: roving tabindex, Arrow/Home/End with RTL-aware arrows, focus moves to the Playground tab on "Edit live" (guide.ts:306-403, verified).
Copy buttons that copy exactly the shown code and announce "Copied to clipboard" in a live region (verified for the main and ready-example blocks).
Focus moved to #main on in-app navigation and filter state preserved when returning to the catalogue (verified).
Explicit disclaimers in guide data (e.g. "No route loader, authentication, government asset entitlement or DGA certification is implied.", component-layout-guides.ts:140).
Pinned Hugeicons Stroke Rounded glyphs for guide icons (guide-icons.ts header) and mirrored directional arrows; framework logos in the compatibility strip.
Scrollable API table wrapper as a named focusable region; code blocks as focusable named regions with dir="ltr".
Ready-to-use examples in four frameworks whose imports and Angular selectors/slots all resolve to real exports (436 blocks checked) - as source material for complete editor projects.
Prev/next component pagination and related components, reduced to links.
drop: All per-page boilerplate sections and intros (guide.ts:233-239): move API, lifecycle, accessibility, framework notes and limitations to a generated per-component Markdown reference.
Separate Preview sample vs Code usage (two examples per page); one example, shown, run and edited.
Variant/Size/Tone/Style selects that edit the first DOM match (guide.ts:190-201) and the guide-only Surface backgrounds and dark button surface (#14573a).
Guide CSS that restyles components inside previews (expansion.css:79-98, demo-previews.css:31-32, guide.css:19); isolate examples instead.

Slogan headings and taglines: "One foundation. Four frameworks.", "Real components. Real interaction.", "Try Tab, arrows & Escape", "Build the next piece", "Keep the foundation. Extend through tokens.", "Ready to make your own", catalogue H1 "Defined for every state."
Related cards that repeat other pages' summaries (4072 words in English across the catalogue).
Fully interactive previews in every catalogue card (628 tab stops, 122 landmarks); use static thumbnails with one link.
Hand-written API tables; generate from the adapters.
Inline style attributes and comment-only imports in copyable code.
notChecked: Screen-reader output (NVDA/VoiceOver) was not run; roles, names and live regions were checked through the DOM and axe only. Whether the re-rendered role=status result count is announced after each filter change is not verified.

Phone-width (390/320) checks were run on 14 component pages (button, text-field, select, combobox, date-picker, tabs, pagination, dialog, alert, data-table, carousel, portal-header, grid, upload) plus the catalogue; the other 69 pages rely on the pre-captured desktop guide-page screenshots.
axe was run on the same 14 pages at 1440px in en/ar x light/dark and on the catalogue from the pre-captured evidence; not on all 83 pages.
API accuracy was reviewed by hand for 29 components; the other 54 rely on the compare.cjs heuristic (name mentions only, not type or default correctness).
The Playground/editor panel behaviour is covered by the editor unit; here only its tab activation and focus were checked.
Comparison of page content with the DGA Platforms Code component guidance: not verifiable from in-repo references at page level (docs/dga-*.md were not compared item by item in this unit).
Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode and 400 % browser zoom (approximated by the 320px reflow) were not tested separately; text-only 200 % zoom passed on 4 pages and the catalogue (zoom.cjs).

Four frameworks." with JavaScript/React/Vue/Angular links to #docs/<fw>.

Demo (guide.ts:222-231, all 83): tabs Preview / Code / Playground + Copy button; Preview canvas (sample(id,"reference")); controls: [Variant+Size on button/icon-button | Tone on alert/badge/chip | Style on button-group], Direction RTL/LTR, Surface Grid/Plain/Soft, Reset; Code panel: H2 "Use this recipe" + "Load the shared stylesheet..." + guide.usage; Playground panel (lazy editor); footnote "Real components. Real interaction." / "Try Tab, arrows & Escape".

3. Variants & composition (guide.ts:233, 50 pages): chips of variant notes.
4. API & markup contract (guide.ts:234, 83 pages): intro sentence + 3-column table Name / Type / Purpose (1-10 rows, median 4).
5. From mount to cleanup (guide.ts:235, 83): intro sentence + ordered lifecycle list.
6. An experience more people can use (guide.ts:236, 83): intro sentence + accessibility checklist.
7. At home in your framework (guide.ts:237, 83): framework notes (40 pages) or a generic sentence (43 pages), React/Vue/Angular "Setup guide" + "API reference" (README on GitHub) links, small note.
8. Know the boundaries (guide.ts:238, 35 pages): limitations list.
9. Build the next piece (guide.ts:239, 83): related component cards repeating each related page summary.

Aside (guide.ts:241): "ON THIS PAGE" with 6 fixed buttons (Examples?, Usage, API & markup, Lifecycle, Accessibility, Frameworks; Variants, Boundaries and Related are never listed) + "Keep the foundation. Extend through tokens." link.

guide:shell-home.summary: Audit of the guide shell (sidebar, top bar, breadcrumb, language switch, mobile drawer, footer, skip link), global search, #overview, #foundations and index.html, in Arabic and English, light and dark, at 1440, 390 and 320 px. No prohibited claims (official DGA product or certification) were found, and the npm install commands match the published 0.2.1 packages. The main problems for the rebuild: (1) the language switch drops keyboard focus to <body>; (2) the shell re-implements skip link, drawer, breadcrumb, icon buttons, toast and footer with guide-only CSS/JS although the packages ship them, and the home restyles package components and pins its preview to light mode; (3) the H1 and title shorten the required wording to "Built to the DGA Platforms Code" / "وفق كود المنصات", slogan copy runs through the shell, home and foundations, and a government attribution sits at the top of every page with no disclaimer; (4) there is no colour-mode control, and direction can be changed apart from locale only by a foundations select that mutates the whole guide; (5) search omits templates and misses common Arabic forms; (6) 22 of 38 guide icons, all from the pinned Hugeicons commit, are not shipped by @hawiyah/styles; (7) first paint waits for a 294 KB-gzip bundle because the HTML has no content. Mobile navigation, the search combobox semantics, reduced-motion handling, 320px reflow and contrast are sound and worth keeping.
keep: Mobile navigation behaviour as a specification for the package drawer: focus goes to Close on open, Tab is contained, Escape and the backdrop close it, focus returns to the toggle, the background is inert and scroll is locked (shell-2.mjs, both languages).

The search combobox pattern (role=combobox + listbox + grouped options + aria-activedescendant + polite result count + focus return), folding of Arabic diacritics and alef forms, and matching across languages (date = تاريخ, hijri = هجري).
An npm-first quick start with a per-framework picker, a correct install command (verified against the npm registry at 0.2.1) and the CSS import in each snippet.
prefers-reduced-motion handling: all shell and home transitions are set to 0 or 1e-05s, the hero tilt is removed and the search animation is set to none. There is no startup loader.
The NIC logo dark-mode rule (experience.css:14) and the light/dark wordmark swap.
Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320px on #overview or #foundations in either language, and skip link to <main> as the first Tab stop.

The foundations page uses package classes (hw-type data-scale, hw-line-clamp, hw-field, hw-select) and real tokens (--hw-shadow-*, --hw-space-*). The override example values match dga-foundations.json.
Contrast of shell and home text: every measured pair is ≥ 4.5:1 in light and dark.
Lead sentence wording: "built to comply with the Digital Government Authority Platforms Code" / "مبنية للامتثال لكود المنصات".
drop: Guide-only shell components (skip-link, sidebar drawer, breadcrumb-top, icon-button, toast, page-footer). Use the package components.
guide-home.css overrides on .hw-button/.hw-input/.hw-progress/.hw-tab/.hw-card and the forced light hero stage.
The global decorateFrameworkMentions text rewriter.
Slogan headings and taglines ("Made for the way you build.", "Configurable within the standard.", "Clarity, woven together.", etc.).
The hand-maintained search index and the duplicated topic list. Generate them from the content source.
The direction select that mutates the whole guide. Scope direction to examples.
Hash routing, the forced scroll-to-top on history navigation, and the silent fallback of unknown routes to the home page.
The repeated licence, version and "Platforms Code" badges. State each once.
Unused font-face imports (Inter, IBM Plex Sans) on routes that never request them.
Decorative "01 / 03", "LIVE PREVIEW" and numbered feature cards.
notChecked: Real screen-reader output (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack). Only names, roles, states, live regions and focus were checked programmatically.
Text spacing (WCAG 1.4.12) and 200% browser text zoom. Reflow was checked at 320 CSS px only.
Forced-colors / Windows High Contrast rendering. Rules exist in playground.css:162 and experience.css:7 but were not run.

Target-size spacing exceptions for the 16-22px-high standalone links ("Explore foundations", "Source on GitHub", footer link). The capture lists them under smallTargets, but the 24px spacing circle was not computed.
Whether the NIC attribution is factually accurate: not verifiable from in-repo references.
Whether the hero focus indicator of .hw-input (a border-colour change) meets 1.4.11 non-text contrast is a package-level question, left to the component audit.
Throttled-network timing. Timings are local and unthrottled; byte sizes are exact.
Comparison of shell layout or tone with the live DGA design portal: not verifiable from in-repo references.

guide:docs-articles.summary: All 12 articles were audited in Arabic and English, light and dark, at 1440, 390 and 320 px. Technical content is largely accurate: tokens, density heights, motion, breakpoints, the Umm al-Qura range and the DGA source values match the packages and in-repo records. The React, Vue and Angular samples compile against packages/*/dist (Angular with strictTemplates), and the React and Vue samples render through SSR. No prohibited claim was found, and Alignment correctly disclaims endorsement and certification. The main problems are newcomer paths: Getting started still says the npm release has not happened, the framework pages have no install or peer-version steps and open with monorepo-only commands, and the JavaScript path silently needs a bundler (verified: tokens.css 404 and an unresolved module without one). All article furniture is guide-only CSS and JS re-implementing shipped components (hw-table-wrap, hw-content-nav, hw-alert, hw-stepper). Other issues: Arabic/English drift in Calendars and Alignment, inconsistent Arabic terminology, marketing taglines and chrome, facts duplicated in 3 to 8 places, samples stored twice with no compile test, identical code-region landmarks, and icons breaking inline links. Keyboard, focus, 320px reflow and reduced motion pass.
keep: Accurate, verified technical content: theme, mode and density attributes, control heights, motion tokens, breakpoints, calendar range and ISO date-only rule, and the DGA source values (see tables.factChecks)
Code samples that compile and render against the real packages (React, Vue, Angular strictTemplates). Keep them as compiled files in the rebuild.
The Alignment disclaimer "Neither the theme nor this source record is an endorsement, certification, or guarantee of complete conformity", and the per-product evaluation framing
The calendars rule set (stored ISO value, explicit out-of-range message, no timezone conversion, numeral style independent of direction) and the civil versus religious calendar caveat
The "RTL is a layout choice; Arabic is a language" guidance, with lang and dir independent and logical CSS
The ownership rule "one owner per DOM subtree": never run the vanilla enhancer over framework-rendered trees
Code blocks forced to dir=ltr and inline code with unicode-bidi:isolate inside Arabic text (verified on all Arabic pages)
Focus to <main> on route change, focusable scroll regions for code and tables, and no horizontal page scroll at 320px
The lifecycle model (create, connect, interact, update, dispose) and the value-ownership table, as a short concept page
drop: The stale "before the npm release ... Do not assume registry packages ..." paragraph
Repository-only "Run the example" steps as the opening of the framework pages; move them to a contributor page
Taglines, "Ready to make your own" code labels, the "Guide · DGA Platforms Code" symbol, the chapter counter and the per-article licence footer
Guide-only .guide-note, .guide-choice, .guide-lifecycle, .guide-table-wrap and .guide-outline; use the shipped hw-alert, hw-card, hw-stepper or hw-timeline, hw-table-wrap and hw-content-nav
Node-level DGA values and template frame IDs in the guide; link docs/dga-reference.md instead
Hand-maintained duplicate Arabic code samples, and restated counts and ranges that live in package READMEs
Inline framework logos in prose
notChecked: Screen-reader output (NVDA, VoiceOver) was not run. Names, roles and landmarks were checked from DOM and axe only.

Whether Angular CLI resolves the bare @import inside styles.css when styles.css is listed in angular.json was not built (no Angular CLI app was created, by the no-install rule). The no-bundler failure is verified.

The npm-published 0.2.1 tarballs were not downloaded. Samples were checked against packages/*/dist built locally at 2026-11-10 12:00, after the last commit. Equivalence to the registry tarballs is not verified.
Comparison of article guidance with the live DGA Platforms Code site: not verifiable from in-repo references (design.dga.gov.sa unreachable). In-repo records were used.
Lifecycle claims about Combobox (typing clears a committed selection; closes on blur) and consent persistence were not exercised in the browser.
Windows high-contrast or forced-colors rendering of the articles was not checked.
Arabic wording judgements (register, terminology) are marked medium confidence and need a native technical editor.

guide:templates-1.summary: Audited the template gallery and the home, home-information, search, service, form and life-journeys templates in Arabic and English, light and dark, at 1440/390/320 px, in the guide and in the full-width preview. The pages are accessible in the main: axe reports no violations in 64 captured variants, nothing scrolls horizontally at 320 px, every keyboard stop has a visible indicator (fields use the DGA underline, confirmed by pixel change), menu Escape returns focus, tabs follow direction, and the form keeps drafts and moves focus to each step heading. Fictional content is clearly labelled and there are no seals, stamps or certification claims. The main problem for the rebuild is honest rendering: 16 visual blocks are guide-only CSS (10 of them duplicate an existing package component such as PortalLayout, PageHeader, SearchField, Feedback, Stat, Grid, Collapsible), 4 package components are restyled by guide CSS (the portal-header mobile menu works only through dga-templates.css), and pagination and accordion use package classes with non-package markup. Template deviations from the recorded guidance: search lacks typing suggestions and shows the clear action when empty, service headings differ from the mandated terms, validation shows browser-language bubbles only. P0: 0, P1: 6, P2: 20, P3: 2.
keep: One fictional but coherent scenario (building permit: service -> form -> confirmation -> rating) that links the templates into a journey
Form behaviour: draft preserved across review/edit, focus moved to each step heading, review summary, local reference number clearly marked HW-DEMO

The feedback template has 11 words of its own and should be dropped; participation, cookies (as a banner plus preferences) and a rewritten content page earn a place.

Breadcrumb, footer and header usage of the package classes; working keyboard menu with Escape and focus return.

guide:labs-journeys.summary: Layout studio and input lab render the package primitives honestly (layoutStyles + hw-* classes; input lab 373 hw-* elements vs 3 guide-only), reflow cleanly at 320px and pass axe in both modes, but the studio exposes 5 of 12 primitives with partly inert controls, and the input lab overstates "22 native input types" (18 are native; date/month/week/datetime-local are a custom DatePicker plus guide-only JavaScript) and ignores Arabic-Indic digit input. The three journeys work end to end and are clearly marked as fictional, but they are mostly guide-only replicas of shipped components, lose keyboard focus to <body> after most actions, recreate their live regions on every render, rely on English browser validation bubbles in the Arabic UI, lack autocomplete on applicant fields, and duplicate the Search/Service/Form templates. No prohibited claims were found on these pages. Recommendation: drop discover and apply, rebuild the workspace as a request-tracking template on DataTable/Pagination/Stat, and keep the layout studio and the input-type reference in a rebuilt, package-only form.
keep: Layout studio principle: the preview and the shown code are produced from the same layoutStyles() call in @hawiyah/core with hw-* classes (codeMatch=true for every pattern); rebuild it on the Angular hw-* layout components with all 12 primitives and a resizable frame for breakpoints.
Per-type semantics table for native inputs (docs/coverage.md) as the single Markdown reference, with honest counts.
Input lab privacy behaviour: values stay local, password redacted in the FormData dump, files reported by name/size/type only.
Demonstration conventions: "No requests are sent", explicit declaration checkbox, "Demo reference HW-DEMO-1043", fictional email hint, data that never leaves the tab.
Moving focus to the new step heading on step change and to the H1 on completion; dialogs that focus Close on open and return focus to the trigger on Escape (verified in both locales).
Draft save/load kept local and explicit; draft survives a locale switch.
Workspace content as the basis of a "request tracking" template (status, reference, timeline) built from DataTable, Pagination, Stat, Timeline, Dialog as shipped.
Logical CSS and mirrored directional icons; Latin identifiers (references, email, code) isolated with dir="ltr".
drop: Discover and apply journeys as separate pages: they duplicate the search, service and form templates with guide-only replicas.

Guide-only component replicas and overrides: .service-card, .search-field, .filter-chip, .page-pagination, .app-stepper, .metric, .request-timeline, .toast, .icon-button, and playground.css rules that resize package components (.form-grid .hw-input, .requests-table .hw-badge, .form-actions .hw-button, ...).
The input-temporal.ts month/week/datetime-local projections unless they become package features.
The "22 native input types" claim in README.md, guide-home.ts and docs/coverage.md until the count matches what is rendered.
Whole-shell innerHTML re-rendering that drops focus and recreates live regions.
Slogan headlines ("A little structure. Endless possibilities.", "A good beginning.") and the "EXPERIENCE / 0n" eyebrows.
Hard-coded metrics and the guide-only .layout-demo-tile class in copied code.
notChecked: Real screen-reader output (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver/TalkBack) for the live regions, toasts and stepper; conclusions on announcements are inferred from DOM behaviour.
Zoom to 200% text-only resizing (only 320px reflow and phone widths were measured).
Mobile virtual keyboards for inputmode/type hints (no device available); only attributes were checked.

guide:brand.summary: Brand material audited: /#brand in main.ts, brand/index.html, brand/index-en.html, brand.css, fonts.css, README.md, decision.json, palette.json, the assets, the kit, and the packaging path through @hawiyah/styles. No P0: there is no official-product or certification claim, and the disclaimers are formal. The identity rules hold: the logo is paths only, no logo font or third-party host is requested, the documented contrast ratios are correct, and the font hashes match. Main defects: dark-mode contrast failure of the /#brand numerals (3.06:1); infinitely looping loader specimens with no pause control; the green wordmark on dark in /#brand; marketing copy in /#brand; descriptions that drift from 'a UI component library built to comply with'; a 'DGA Platforms Code' label on the logo panel; static pages without dark mode that share nothing with the packages; alias versus canonical asset names contradicting each other between the docs and the package (about 373 KB of duplicate files in the tarball); three different loader recipes; and facts repeated in up to 11 files.
keep: Wordmark as outlined SVG paths: every asset uses <path> only (no <text>, no font reference). No logo font is requested at runtime: /#brand and both static pages made 0 requests matching 'aref', and every request went to 127.0.0.1 (no third-party hosts).
Generators: brand/build-assets.py (HarfBuzz, offline) and brand/build-loader.mjs (Chromium + ffmpeg) are the documented regeneration path; GIFs measured at 90 frames, 3.6 s, as documented.
Font provenance: SHA-256 of all bundled TTF/OFL files matches third-party/sources.json; the OFL notices sit next to each font.

All eight documented contrast ratios in palette.json and the pages are correct (recomputed; for example white on primary 4.75, primary text on dark 7.79). All brand hex values exist in @hawiyah/tokens.
The reduced-motion <picture> fallback for the loader works (currentSrc switches to the static SVG). The static pages turn off smooth scroll under reduced motion.

spike:angular-guide.verdict: Viable as an architecture, but not with the unpatched 0.2.1 packages. From the registry, unpatched: install, the stylesheet/asset chain under /hawiyah/, strict AOT of all 87 concrete exports (0 errors), prerender + hydration of 75 of 83 catalog components, deep links, 404.html, route-level locale with independent direction and mode, and 48 interactive components after hydration all work. Blockers, all in @hawiyah/angular and @hawiyah/core: hw-tabs and hw-content-navigation throw an uncaught exception from a timer during server rendering, which fails the whole `ng build` (97 of 192 routes written, 91 route errors) and ends `ng serve`; toggle-group, combobox, tag-input, multi-select, date-picker and accordion throw in lifecycle hooks on the server, leaving incomplete HTML while the build exits 0 (and failing the build when ngModel/formControl is used); and hw-tabs cannot be hydrated (NG0509) even once server rendering is shimmed. Generated ids also differ between server and client on 26 of 88 pages. A package release fixing GAP-1 to GAP-5 is required before an honest guide can prerender every component.

spike:editor-runtime.verdict: Viable. A live editor can run the PUBLISHED @hawiyah/* 0.2.1 packages (registry install, no links or aliases) in JavaScript, React, Vue and Angular inside <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms" srcdoc> under a strict CSP, and it works inside an Angular 22 application built with AOT, strict templates and prerendering under /hawiyah/. Evidence: 24 of 24 strategy x framework combinations render; all 83 recipes of today's guide in four frameworks (332 previews) render in each delivery configuration except one recipe that points at a guide-only image; the delivery strategy leaves the rendered DOM unchanged (331 of 331); the 476 @hawiyah files served are byte-identical to the npm tarballs, also after ng build. Recommended: strategy (b), published files through an import map, with the official Angular linker applied at guide build time (JIT-linking the published FESM in the browser works but costs 0.4-0.8 s per preview), pre-bundles only for React and rxjs, one stylesheet made by CONCATENATING the published files (the bundler's flat output rendered 6 of 331 previews differently), the frame's code shipped as a static asset (Function#toString of code compiled by Angular fails in the frame), examples precompiled and compilers loaded on first edit. Measured price against per-framework bundles: 30-80 ms locally and 125-160 ms at 40 ms latency on the first preview of vanilla/React/Vue, nothing on re-runs, a gain for Angular. What blocks an honest result is in the packages and in the guide's own preview CSS: the @hawiyah/styles entry cannot be loaded by a browser as published (G1); the packages publish no page-level base and the base rules of today's preview frame change 160 of 331 screenshots against the published stylesheet alone (G18); and the adapters do not render the same structure for the same component (33 differences in the proof example although its four screenshots are pixel-identical; with today's recipes the three adapters agree on the hw- contract in 16 of 83 components). Open risk: only Chromium could be tested; if import maps with data: modules in sandboxed srcdoc frames fail in Firefox or Safari, fall back to strategy (a) with the bundle fetched by the frame.
